FINAL ANSWER — DA-1-3: Cell-subset distribution across tumor, adjacent normal, and peripheral blood, and the subsets specifically enriched only in the tumor microenvironment

COHORT ANALYZED
975,275 cells, 169 samples, 22 patients from the CRC anti-PD-1 cohort (GSE236581): 58 tumor samples (279,886 cells), 52 adjacent-normal samples (260,294 cells), 56 peripheral-blood samples (417,162 cells), pooled across treatment stages I-IV (2 LN and 1 TN sample, 17,933 cells, excluded from statistics as unreplicated). 91 annotated cell subsets in 6 lineages. All statistics below use per-sample subset proportions; inference uses per-patient averages (22 patients, all three tissues available for every patient), paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR across the 91 subsets.

1) COMPARTMENT COMPOSITION (mean % of cells per sample; lineage level)
- Peripheral blood: T cells 64.4%, myeloid 14.1% (CD14 monocytes alone 7.4%), B cells 10.7%, ILC 10.1%, epithelial 0.6%, stromal 0.2%. Dominant subsets: naive/central-memory CD4 (c01_CD4_Tn_CCR7 10.6%, c02_Tn_SELL 6.4%, c04_Tcm_ANXA1 5.8%), CD8_Temra_CX3CR1 (6.7%), CD8_Temra_TYROBP (4.1%), Mono_CD14 (7.4%), Mono_FCGR3A (2.2%), ILC_FCGR3A (4.8%), NaiveB_TCL1A (4.5%).
- Adjacent normal mucosa: epithelial 37.9% (colonocytes c84 15.7%, goblet c87 6.0%), B/plasma 23.7% (IgA plasma cells c46_PlasmaB_IGHA1 17.8% - the single most normal-specific population), T cells 27.2% (dominated by tissue-resident CD8_Trm_XCL1 2.4% and CD8_IEL_CD160 2.1%), stromal 8.4% (Fibro_ADAMDEC1 2.8%, Fibro_SOX6 1.1%).
- Tumor: T cells 40.9%, epithelial 29.5%, B/plasma 16.2%, stromal 6.7%, myeloid 4.9% (highest myeloid fraction of the two tissue sites), ILC 1.8%. Most abundant subsets: c84_Coloncyte_CA2 6.0%, c46_PlasmaB_IGHA1 4.2%, c20_CD8_Tem_GZMK 3.7%, c90_Epi_MKI67 3.4%, c05_CD4_Tcm_GPR183 3.1%, c87_Goblet_MUC2 3.0%, c91_Epi_Tumor 2.7%.
- Classification of all 91 subsets by the same rule applied symmetrically: 5 tumor-specific, 5 normal-enriched (c46_PlasmaB_IGHA1, c73_Fibro_ADAMDEC1, c21_CD8_Trm_XCL1, c86_Coloncyte_BEST4, c72_Fibro_SOX6), 20 blood-enriched, 61 shared/low-abundance.

2) SUBSETS SPECIFICALLY AND HIGHLY ENRICHED ONLY IN THE TUMOR MICROENVIRONMENT
Criteria (pre-stated, all four required): median proportion >= 0.5% in tumor; fold-change >= 4 vs BOTH normal and blood; paired Wilcoxon BH-q < 0.05 vs BOTH; median <= 0.5% in BOTH normal and blood.

RANK 1 - c13_CD4_Treg_TNFRSF9 (activated tumor Treg): tumor median 2.36% (mean 2.8%) vs normal 0.28%, blood ~0 (median 0). FC 8.1x vs normal, 237x vs blood; q = 5.5e-05 and 1.3e-06. Detected in 58/58-sample terms in 98% of tumor samples and in 22/22 patients. Raw-count validation: FOXP3 68.8%, CTLA4 71.1%, TIGIT 78.5%, IL2RA 55.2%, LAYN 55.7%, TNFRSF9 42.4% - the top rung of a clean activation ladder across Treg subsets (TNFRSF9 3.3% in c11 -> 16.0% in c12 -> 42.4% in c13).

RANK 2 - c23_CD8_Tex_LAYN (terminally exhausted CD8 T cells): tumor median 1.63% (mean 3.9%) vs normal 0.06%, blood ~0. FC 23.0x / 164x; q = 1.4e-04 / 1.3e-06; 22/22 patients. Validation: LAYN 36.8%, CXCL13 53.9%, HAVCR2 37.7%, PDCD1 35.0%, ENTPD1 32.3%, GZMB 88.3% with GZMK only 33.0% (vs circulating c19_CD8_Tem_CMC1: LAYN 0.2%, GZMK 81.2%).

RANK 3 - c27_CD8_MAIT_SLC4A10 (tissue/tumor-resident MAIT cells): tumor median 1.13% (mean 1.9%) vs normal 0.21%, blood ~0. FC 5.1x / 114x; q = 7.2e-04 / 1.3e-06; 22/22 patients; present in 100% of tumor AND normal samples (a mucosal lineage whose abundance nevertheless concentrates 5-fold in tumor). Validation: KLRB1 93.0%, SLC4A10 30.7%, ZBTB16 37.7%, with tumor-acquired activation LAYN 30.1%, PDCD1 24.1% (blood MAIT c26: LAYN 0.7%, PDCD1 2.8%).

RANK 4 - c07_CD4_Th17_CTSH (tumor Th17 cells): tumor median 0.68% (mean 1.4%) vs normal 0.13%, blood ~0. FC 4.9x / 69x; q = 5.5e-05 / 1.3e-06; 22/22 patients. Validation: KLRB1 77.6%, CTSH 45.5%, RORC 8.7%, IL17A 9.2%, IL23R 9.6%, PDCD1 33.6%.

RANK 5 - c09_CD4_Th1_CXCL13_HAVCR2 (CXCL13+ HAVCR2+ Th1-like helper T cells): tumor median 0.61% (mean 1.3%) vs normal 0.02%, blood ~0. FC 22.9x / 62x; q = 5.5e-05 / 1.3e-06; 22/22 patients. Validation: CXCL13 68.1%, HAVCR2 19.2%, PDCD1 48.1%, CTLA4 54.2%, TIGIT 53.0%.

Together these five subsets constitute, on average, ~28% of all CD4 tumor-infiltrating T
cells (c13+c07+c09) and ~19% of all CD8 tumor-infiltrating T cells (c23) while being
essentially absent from blood (median 0%) and 5–23-fold depleted relative to the patient's
own adjacent normal mucosa. They form one coherent program: antigen-experienced, chronically
stimulated, PD-1-axis (PDCD1/CTLA4/TIGIT/LAYN/CXCL13) T-cell states that the tumor
microenvironment selectively accumulates.

3) TUMOR-ASSOCIATED BUT NOT TUMOR-SPECIFIC (important distinctions)
- c91_Epi_Tumor (malignant epithelium): tumor 2.70% vs normal 1.38% (FC only 1.95; q_vs_normal 1.8e-04) - enriched vs normal but NOT tumor-specific, because normal mucosa is epithelium-dominated by construction. Its tumor-restricted nature is qualitative, not proportional.
- Mucosa-shared populations (fail specificity because normal is equal or higher): c84_Coloncyte_CA2 (tumor 5.99% vs normal 15.73%), c87_Goblet_MUC2 (3.04% vs 6.00%), c46_PlasmaB_IGHA1 (4.17% vs 17.75%), c90_Epi_MKI67 (3.40% vs 3.26%), c20_CD8_Tem_GZMK (3.69% vs 2.05%).
- Strongly tumor-skewed but below the 0.5% abundance floor (would join the list at a 0.1% floor): c70_Endo_COL4A1 (0.42%, tumor-only, FC 43), c79_Fibro_FAP (0.14%, CAF, FC 15, FAP+ 73.2%), c63_Mph_CCL20 (0.11%, FC 12), c55_pDC_GZMB (0.10%, FC 11), c62_Mph_S100A8 (0.21%, FC 5.7), c64_Mph_SPP1 (0.05%, SPP1+ 45.4%, FC 6.3), c60_cDC_LAMP3 (0.06%, LAMP3+ 95.9%, mature DC, FC 4.7). These are genuine tumor-microenvironment-restricted stromal/myeloid populations of low frequency.
- Near-misses on the FC-vs-normal criterion only: c34_ILC_NR4A2 (tumor 1.22% vs normal 0.41%, FC 3.0) and c08_CD4_Tfh_CXCL13_IL6ST (0.68% vs 0.29%, FC 2.3) - tumor-enriched mucosal states rather than tumor-specific ones.

4) ROBUSTNESS
- Results hold restricted to pre-treatment samples only (stage I): c13 2.64%, c23 1.62%, c27 1.43%, c07 0.71%, c09 0.48% - so the calls are not an on-treatment artifact.
- Unpaired Mann-Whitney U agrees with the paired Wilcoxon for all five calls.
- Every called subset is detected in the tumor of 22/22 patients (c64_Mph_SPP1 21/22).
- Marker evidence comes from the raw UMI matrix (streamed 19 GB MatrixMarket parse, 65-gene panel), with cell/gene alignment independently verified: per-cell column UMI sums match metadata nCount_RNA for 975,227/975,275 cells (max |diff| 18); an EPCAM single-gene sweep places 91.0% of EPCAM+ cells in annotated epithelium (per-sample r = 0.958); positive controls pass (LYZ 99.7% in c49_Mono_CD14, MUC2 95.8% in c87_Goblet_MUC2, MKI67 78.1% in c29_T_MKI67, IGHA1 93.0% in c46_PlasmaB_IGHA1, FAP 73.2% in c79_Fibro_FAP).

5) LIMITATIONS
Cell-type labels are the data release's annotations (no re-clustering); blood-vs-tissue differences partly reflect sampling/dissociation (blood draw vs colonoscopy/surgery), which is why tumor-specificity calls rest on immune subsets recoverable from all compartments; proportions are compositional and fold-changes vs blood use a +1e-4 pseudocount on medians (blood FCs of 62-237x mean "median blood fraction = 0"); the 0.5%/4x/q<0.05 thresholds are conventional and the near-miss list quantifies sensitivity; no response-stratified (CR/PR/SD) or causal claims are made here.

SUMMARY SENTENCE
The tumor microenvironment is distinguished from both adjacent normal mucosa and peripheral blood by the selective accumulation of activated/exhausted, PD-1-axis T-cell states - activated TNFRSF9-hi Tregs (c13, median 2.36% of tumor cells), exhausted LAYN+CXCL13+ CD8 T cells (c23, 1.63%), tumor-resident MAIT cells (c27, 1.13%), Th17 cells (c07, 0.68%), and CXCL13+HAVCR2+ Th1-like helpers (c09, 0.61%) - each 5-23x enriched over adjacent normal and essentially absent from blood (22/22 patients, BH-q < 1e-03), with lower-frequency tumor-restricted stromal/myeloid populations (FAP+ CAF, SPP1+ and CCL20+ macrophages, LAMP3+ mature DC, COL4A1+ endothelium) below the 0.5% abundance floor.
grader_notes: The analysis is rigorous and well-documented but does not restrict to baseline only, and its abundance threshold excludes expected myeloid/stromal tumor-specific subpopulations from the top list, causing several B-level ratings.

FINAL ANSWER — DA-1-4: Correlation between tumor regression ratio and baseline cell-subtype proportions (GSE236581, n = 22 CRC ICB patients)

METHOD (one correlation per subtype across patients; "for each patient" supplies the per-patient values that enter each correlation)
- Baseline = pre-treatment biopsies (Treatment stage "I", confirmed "Pre"/"Baseline" in clinical.xlsx); primary compartment = tumor (105,959 cells; one baseline tumor sample per patient; median 4,789 cells/patient).
- For each patient, SubCellType proportions were computed from the 91 annotated clusters; each subtype's per-patient proportion vector was correlated with the per-patient Tumor Regression Ratio (TRR, -0.026 to 1.000; 12 CR, 7 PR, 3 SD) using Spearman rank correlation (plus Pearson, BH-FDR over 91 tests, and MSI/MSS-adjusted partial Spearman as sensitivity analyses).

DIRECTION OF THE CORRELATIONS — BOTH SIGNS OCCUR, IN A BIOLOGICALLY COHERENT PATTERN

POSITIVE correlations (higher baseline proportion -> more regression -> better response):
- c23_CD8_Tex_LAYN (exhausted CD8 T cells): rho = +0.506, p = 0.016 (MSI-adjusted p = 0.019); present in all 22 patients (3,832 cells). Most robust association.
- c13_CD4_Treg_TNFRSF9 (activated/tumor-antigen-experienced Treg): rho = +0.470, p = 0.027 (adjusted p = 0.035); all 22 patients (3,498 cells).
- Combined tumor-reactive T fraction (Tex + TNFRSF9+ Treg): rho = +0.477, p = 0.025.
- c68_Endo_FABP5 (endothelium): rho = +0.502, p = 0.017; c82_SMC_MYH11 (smooth muscle): rho = +0.536, p = 0.010 (few cells: 64/139 — directional support only).
- All-tissue baseline adds tertiary-lymphoid-structure populations: c44_GCB_MKI67 rho = +0.589 (p = 0.004), c43_GCB_LRMP +0.470, c08_CD4_Tfh_CXCL13 +0.440, c46_PlasmaB_IGHA1 +0.405.

NEGATIVE correlations (higher baseline proportion -> less regression -> poorer response):
- c87_Goblet_MUC2 (normal-like goblet epithelium): rho = -0.464, p = 0.030 (adjusted p = 0.033; 5,985 cells, 21/22 patients).
- Aggregated normal-like epithelium (goblet + colonocytes + enterocytes etc.): rho = -0.486, p = 0.022.
- c84_Coloncyte_CA2: rho = -0.351; c45_PlasmaB_TXNDC5: rho = -0.353; B-lineage subtypes overall skew negative (2/10 positive).
- Malignant epithelium itself is NOT correlated (rho = +0.184, p = 0.41); major-lineage proportions are all non-significant (T +0.22, Epi -0.20, others ~0).

Of 91 subtypes, 6 reach nominal p < 0.05 (5 positive, 1 negative); none survive FDR < 0.05 across 91 tests (min q = 0.36) at n = 22. Direction split across the 62 well-detected subtypes: 33 positive vs 29 negative (sign-test p = 0.70). Associations are unchanged after MSI/MSS adjustment and leave-one-out (all headline LOO ranges exclude 0).

WHAT THIS IMPLIES
1. Sign of the immune signal is POSITIVE: tumors that regress most under anti-PD-1 therapy are those whose BASELINE microenvironment is already enriched for terminally differentiated exhausted CD8 T cells (LAYN+ Tex) and activated TNFRSF9+ Tregs — i.e., a pre-existing, chronically antigen-stimulated ("hot"/pre-primed) T-cell response. PD-1 blockade re-invigorates pre-primed tumor-reactive T cells rather than recruiting new ones, so baseline Tex/Treg content marks an inhibitable infiltrate and predicts pathological regression.
2. Sign of the normal-epithelial signal is NEGATIVE: biopsies dominated by normal-like mucosal epithelium (goblet cells, colonocytes) — effectively a "colder", less immune-dominated or lower-tumor-content biopsy — regress least.
3. Positive GCB/Tfh/plasma-cell correlations point to pre-existing tertiary lymphoid structures as an additional response-favoring feature.
4. Clinical implication: baseline tumor-biopsy cell-subtype composition (high Tex + activated Treg, low normal-like epithelium) is a candidate pretreatment predictor of regression under ICB. No such signal exists in baseline blood in this cohort, so the predictor is tumor-local.

LIMITATIONS
- Only 22 patients (no PD; 3 SD); correlations are nominally significant only and do not survive multiple-testing correction; effect sizes |rho| ~ 0.5 need larger cohorts for confirmation.
- Observational associations; residual confounding by regimen (mono vs chemo-combination), MSI, TMB, stage beyond the MSI adjustment performed.
- Proportions are compositional: the positive-immune/negative-normal-epithelium pattern is partly one axis (immune fraction vs epithelial dilution), and biopsy tumor-cellularity was not available to separate tumor content from biology.
- Rare subtypes (SMC_MYH11, Endo_FABP5) have unstable estimates; raw UMI matrix not reprocessed (provided annotations taken as given).

Files: analysis trace in trace.md; per-patient table per_patient_summary.csv; full correlation tables results_subcelltype_tumor_baseline.csv (91 subtypes), results_subcelltype_tumor_baseline_filtered.csv (62), results_majorcelltype_tumor_baseline.csv; figure fig_subtype_vs_TRR.png.
grader_notes: The analysis is rigorous in baseline filtering, count matrix construction, normalization, merging, and batch correlation, but falls short on rare/zero-variance filtering completeness, top negative candidate identification, and the specificity of negative-correlation biological interpretation. Source reliability is strong.

DA-10-1 FINAL ANSWER
ML screening of membraneless-organelle participants: amino-acid composition of PS-Self (SaPS) vs PS-Part (PdPS) proteins, and benchmark of phase-separation predictors against non-PS (NoPS) proteins.

DATA
sequence_prediction_filtered.xlsx: 48,504 proteins x 23 columns (UniProt index, Organism, Sequence, scores for catGRANULE / PLAAC / PScore, SaPS-8fea / PdPS-8fea / SaPS-10fea / PdPS-10fea classifier probabilities, and 0/1 labels SaPS / hSaPS / PdPS / hPdPS / NoPS / hNoPS). idr_ranges.xlsx: 55,056 IDR segments for 24,451 proteins (UniProt, start, end). Set sizes used: SaPS 128 (58 human), PdPS 214 (93 human), NoPS 48,158 (8,799 human), hSaPS 59, hPdPS 96, hNoPS 8,799; labels mutually exclusive, 4 unlabelled rows excluded. NO FUZDROP SCORES EXIST in the provided data and FuzDrop cannot be installed or reached from this environment (no PyPI package, web server DNS-unreachable); the task rules forbid consulting the source paper. FuzDrop is therefore reported as NOT EVALUABLE; no number below is attributed to it. The dataset's own SaPS/PdPS 8- and 10-feature ML classifiers were analysed as surrogates/comparators (clearly not FuzDrop).

PART 1 - AMINO-ACID COMPOSITION: PS-SELF vs PS-PART
Method: pooled residue fractions per set; per-protein Mann-Whitney U per amino acid; Benjamini-Hochberg FDR over 20 tests; replicated in the human-only sets.

PS-Self (SaPS) are significantly enriched (BH q < 0.05, pan-species) in: Gly (8.88% vs 6.40%, log2FC +0.47), Pro (7.33% vs 6.24%, +0.23), Thr (6.49% vs 5.36%, +0.28, q=0.052), Ser (10.28% vs 9.13%, +0.17), Gln (+0.12); grouped Gly+Pro 16.2% vs 12.6% (p<1e-4) and polar STNQ 27.1% vs 24.0% (p<1e-4).
PS-Part (PdPS) are significantly enriched in: Cys (1.36% vs 0.91%, log2FC -0.57 for SaPS/PdPS), Ile (-0.28), Leu (-0.26), Glu (-0.25), Lys (-0.23), Arg (-0.22), His (-0.22), Asp (-0.15), Val (-0.11); grouped acidic DE 12.7% vs 11.1% (p<1e-4), basic KR 12.4% vs 10.6% (p<1e-4), hydrophobic LIVAM 28.2% vs 25.6% (p<1e-4). Aromatic FYW does not differ (6.6% vs 6.4%, p=0.40).
Human-only replication (hSaPS 59 vs hPdPS 96): same directions for all |log2FC|>0.1 residues - G +0.37 (q<1e-4), P +0.41 (q=3e-4), Q +0.14 (q=0.019), K -0.25 (q=5e-4), E -0.19 (q=0.008), L -0.20 (q=2e-4), I -0.31 (q=1e-4), V -0.09 (q=0.029); Cys and His lose significance at this smaller n.
Against NoPS: BOTH PS classes are Cys-depleted (SaPS/NoPS log2FC -1.10; PdPS/NoPS -0.53; both q<1e-4) and depleted of bulky hydrophobics/aromatics (W -0.71/-0.58; L -0.42/-0.16; I -0.41/-0.13) and enriched in Pro/Q/Ser; but the Gly enrichment (+0.53) is specific to PS-Self (PdPS vs NoPS Gly p=0.83), whereas significant D/E/K/R enrichment vs NoPS is specific to PS-Part (all p<=3e-2, three of them <1e-4).
Disorder: mean annotated IDR fraction SaPS 0.311 > PdPS 0.216 > NoPS 0.110 (human 0.326 / 0.267 / 0.138); >=1 IDR in 90.6% / 81.3% / 50.1% (human 94.9 / 84.4 / 58.4%).
Charge: fraction of charged residues SaPS 0.222 < PdPS 0.261 (MWU p=7.95e-08), but net charge per residue does not differ (p=0.25) - PS-Part carries MORE charge while staying net-neutral; PS-Self is weakly charged.
Interpretation: PS-Self proteins carry the classic self-assembling low-complexity signature (Gly/Ser/Pro/Thr/Gln-rich, Cys-poor, weakly charged, highly disordered) consistent with sticker-spacer self-multivalency; PS-Part proteins are compositionally intermediate toward non-PS proteins - disordered but more hydrophobic (L/I/V) and more strongly charged (K/E/D/R), i.e. they look like ordinary binding proteins carrying partner-interaction motifs, consistent with partner-dependent condensation. Examples (top PScore per class; genes from UniProt): PS-Self TAF15 (18.5), HNRNPDL (16.8), HNRNPA3 (15.7), PRNP (12.9), CIRBP (10.8); PS-Part DDX3X (7.9), SFPQ (7.7), RBMX (6.9), TRA2B (6.9), CAPRIN1 (6.8).

PART 2 - PREDICTOR PERFORMANCE (distinguishing each PS type from non-PS)
Method: ROC-AUC with 2,000-resample bootstrap 95% CI, PR-AUC with prevalence, sensitivity/specificity/PPV at published operating thresholds (PScore >= 4, PLAAC > 0, catGRANULE > 0, classifiers >= 0.5), Mann-Whitney p, Youden-optimal thresholds, IDR-matched-negative sensitivity analysis, IDR-fraction-only naive baseline.

Human benchmark (positives vs hNoPS n=8,799):
- hSaPS (n=59) vs hNoPS: PLAAC AUC 0.831 (0.764-0.894), catGRANULE 0.814 (0.761-0.865), PScore 0.813 (0.754-0.871); at published thresholds PScore>=4: sens 0.424/spec 0.954/PPV 0.064 (8.7x enrichment); PLAAC>0: 0.593/0.926/0.051 (7.6x); catGRANULE>0: 0.966/0.385/0.010 (1.6x). PR-AUC 0.12-0.13 at 0.7% prevalence.
- hPdPS (n=96) vs hNoPS: catGRANULE 0.726 (0.676-0.773), PScore 0.689 (0.636-0.742), PLAAC 0.639 (0.567-0.698); PScore>=4 detects only 19.6% of PdPS (spec 0.954, PPV 0.047, 4.1x); catGRANULE>0 sens 0.875 but spec 0.385 (1.4x enrichment).
- Every published predictor ranks hSaPS significantly above hPdPS (median PScore 3.24 vs 1.98, p=6.8e-04; PLAAC 0.13 vs -0.13, p=1.4e-06; catGRANULE 0.97 vs 0.70, p=7.8e-03); hSaPS vs hPdPS AUCs: PLAAC 0.731, PScore 0.664, catGRANULE 0.628.
- Pan-species replication (SaPS 128 / PdPS 214 / NoPS 48,158): SaPS-vs-NoPS AUC PScore 0.831, PLAAC 0.834, catGRANULE 0.817; PdPS-vs-NoPS 0.663 / 0.644 / 0.706; SaPS-vs-PdPS 0.702 / 0.719 / 0.665.
- Dataset ML classifiers (surrogate for sequence-feature propensity models; likely trained on these labels, so optimistic): SaPS-8fea AUC 0.987 and SaPS-10fea 0.990 for SaPS vs NoPS; PdPS-8fea 0.984 and PdPS-10fea 0.990 for PdPS vs NoPS; cross-type SaPS-8fea separates SaPS from PdPS at AUC 0.918 while PdPS-8fea is anti-correlated (AUC 0.137), i.e. the two classes are nearly disjoint in feature space.
- Youden-optimal cuts (human): PScore 2.12 (hSaPS sens 0.746/spec 0.780), 1.54 (hPdPS 0.620/0.664); PLAAC -0.068 / -0.133; catGRANULE 0.771 / 0.369.
Robustness: restricting negatives to proteins with >=1 IDR lowers AUCs modestly and preserves the ordering (hSaPS: PLAAC 0.790, PScore 0.755, catGRANULE 0.763; hPdPS: catGRANULE 0.695, PScore 0.655, PLAAC 0.613). A naive baseline using only annotated IDR fraction achieves AUC 0.779 (hSaPS) and 0.689 (hPdPS), i.e. most of the published predictors' discrimination is disorder content; the type-specific ML classifiers add ~0.2 AUC beyond disorder (Spearman rho with IDR fraction only 0.36-0.56).

BOTTOM LINE
1) PS-Self and PS-Part proteins differ compositionally, not just in mechanism: PS-Self is Gly/Pro/Ser/Thr(Gln)-rich, Cys-poor, weakly charged and the most disordered; PS-Part is more hydrophobic (L/I/V) and more strongly charged (K/E/D/R) with higher charged-residue fraction but unchanged net charge, sitting between PS-Self and non-PS proteins. Gly enrichment and Cys depletion are the sharpest single-residue discriminators (log2FC +0.47 and -0.57 between the two PS classes).
2) All three evaluated published predictors (PScore, PLAAC, catGRANULE) discriminate PS-Self from non-PS well (AUC 0.81-0.83 human, 0.82-0.83 pan-species) but discriminate PS-Part substantially worse (AUC 0.64-0.73), and all three systematically score PS-Self above PS-Part (p <= 7.8e-03). At the canonical PScore >= 4 cut, ~42% of PS-Self but only ~20% of PS-Part proteins are detected. Absolute PPVs stay low (<= 6%) because positives are rare (0.7-1.1% prevalence).
3) FuzDrop could not be evaluated: no FuzDrop scores are present in the provided files, no installable implementation exists, and its server is unreachable; per task rules the source paper was not consulted. The dataset's own SaPS/PdPS ML classifiers (0.98-0.99 AUC, likely optimistically biased by training-set overlap) show that the self- vs partner-dependent distinction is learnable from sequence features and is nearly symmetric-disjoint, far exceeding the published predictors' 0.63-0.73 AUC for that contrast.
4) Limitations: predictor benchmarking partly measures disorder (IDR fraction alone gives AUC 0.78/0.69); NoPS is "not observed to phase-separate", not "cannot"; the ML classifiers' near-perfect AUCs are likely circular; human-only sets are small (59/96 positives, AUC CIs ~0.10 wide); whole-sequence pooling dilutes low-complexity regions.

Full methods, code, intermediate counts and references: trace.md. Figure: outputs/fig1_composition_predictors.png. Tables: analysis/*.csv. Scripts: analysis/step1_composition.py, step2_predictors.py, step3_figures.py.
grader_notes: The agent performed a mostly thorough analysis with correct data loading, set construction, composition computation, AUC evaluation, and summary, but missed IDR-based amino-acid ordering entirely and did not fully replicate fold-change versus NoPS on human sets.

FINAL ANSWER — ML screening of membraneless organelle (MLO) participants (DA-10-3)

Question: do phase-separation (PS) predictors screen MLO participant datasets consistently better than membrane-bound organelle control datasets, against a fixed non-PS background?

VERDICT: YES in aggregate — every predictor performs better on (nearly) every MLO dataset than on the membrane-bound control, and on the membrane-bound control itself the predictors are at or BELOW chance. The consistency is strong across datasets but NOT across predictors: individual predictors differ widely and several are near chance on specific MLO sets.

SETUP
- Analysis frame: 20,375 human proteins with predictor scores from sequence_prediction.xlsx (catGRANULE, PLAAC, PScore, SaPS-8fea, PdPS-8fea) joined to DeepPhase and class flags (hSaPS 59, hPdPS 96, hNoPS 8,801) from h_combined_with_flags.xlsx and to the six 0/1 dataset flags from List_of_proteins_for_comparing_MLO_enrichment.xlsx (header on row 2; Original data sheet).
- Negative/background = hNoPS (the fixed "hNoPS-test" set), n=8,799 with complete catGRANULE/SaPS-8fea/PdPS-8fea (8,655 PLAAC, 7,970 PScore, 5,202 DeepPhase).
- Positives: OpenCell nuclear punctae 140, DACT1-particulate proteome 264, G3BP1 proximity labeling 285, PhaSepDB high-throughput 1,866, Amyloid fiber-forming 68 (5 MLO/particulate datasets); membrane-bound control = Proteomics of human mitochondri 1,125. Metric: ROC-AUC + AUPRC + one-sided Mann-Whitney p, bootstrap 95% CI (2,000 resamples), plus fold enrichment above the hNoPS 99th/95th percentile.

MAIN RESULTS (ROC-AUC vs hNoPS, Original data sheet)
                  OpenCell  DACT1  G3BP1  PhaSepDB  Amyloid | Mito(control)

This is the expected signature if the scores capture condensate-forming biophysics (prion-like/low-complexity character, pi-pi contacts, granule propensity) rather than generic "being in a proteomics list" or generic disorder/hydrophobicity: membrane-bound-organelle residents are not enriched for condensation propensity.

- Only ONE membrane-bound control dataset (human mitochondrial proteome) exists in the data; "membrane-bound controls" generalization rests on n=1 control dataset, and per-predictor sign tests rest on 5 paired datasets.
- The 30-pair p-values are anti-conservative (predictors share datasets and datasets share predictors); the descriptive 28/30 pattern and per-predictor counts carry the argument.
- Correlation only — no mechanistic claim; the Amyloid fiber-forming set (n=68) shows no significant separation by any predictor, so the conclusion does not extend to amyloid-type aggregates.
- PhaSepDB high-throughput mixes many organelles and 706 of its 2,572 members have no human predictor score (86 are Xenopus entries), so its AUC describes the scorable subset only.
- DeepPhase is scored for only 59% of the background and 15–59 positives per dataset; conclusions using it are fragile.
- SaPS-8fea/PdPS-8fea were trained on curated classes that overlap the evaluation lists; the leakage-reduced sheet mitigates but does not remove this circularity.

BOTTOM LINE
Against a fixed non-PS (hNoPS) background, all six predictors screen MLO participant datasets better than the membrane-bound mitochondrial control (28/30 dataset-predictor pairs; median AUC advantage +0.12; sign-test p = 4.3e-07), and on the membrane-bound control they perform at or significantly below chance (AUC 0.42–0.52, top-1% enrichment <= 0.6x). Consistency holds across datasets but not uniformly across predictors: catGRANULE dominates G3BP1 where PLAAC/PScore fail, PdPS-8fea/SaPS-8fea dominate OpenCell/DACT1/PhaSepDB, and no predictor significantly separates the small amyloid fiber-forming set.

ANSWER — Cell-cell communication between KIR+CD8 T cells and pathogenic (gliadin-specific-like) CD4 T cells in active celiac lesions (GSE193442, 10 duodenal samples: 6 active CeD, 4 healthy controls)

DATA PROCESSED
72,177 raw cells -> QC (300-6,000 genes, >=500 UMIs, <=15% mt) and per-sample Scrublet doublet removal -> 64,567 cells x 18,468 genes. Harmony integration on sample, Leiden clustering. The capture is essentially a T/NK compartment (CD3D+ cells dominate; LYZ, MZB1, COL1A1, EPCAM, MS4A1 all ~0), so all communication reported is T-T.
Populations defined by cell-level gating on detected genes:
- KIR+CD8 T cells: 1,354 cells (752 CeD / 602 HC); 100% CD3D+, 94% CD8A+, 0% TRDC; GZMB 77%, PRF1 84%, GNLY 78%; KIR2DL3 39%, KIR3DL1 38%, KIR3DL2 32%; KLRC2 (NKG2C) 22%, KLRC1 (NKG2A) 11%, LILRB1 17%.
- Activated/pathogenic-like CD4 T cells: CD4+CD3+CD8-TRDC- and HLA-DRA/HLA-DRB1+ (surrogate for gliadin-specific HLA-DQ-restricted effector CD4 clones; no TCR/tetramer data exist in count matrices) = 561 cells (424 CeD / 137 HC).

METHOD
LIANA 1.10 rank-aggregate (CellPhoneDB + Connectome + NATMI + SingleCellSignalR + log2FC consensus; 500 permutations, seed 0) on log-normalised data, using the OmniPath "consensus" resource (4,620 pairs) augmented with 60+ curated KIR/MHC-II/NKG2D/effector pairs that the stock resource lacks; all KIR_CD8 <-> CD4_act/CD4_T directed pairs extracted (613 interactions, 231 non-MHC-I). Independent cell-level evidence: % ligand+ source cells and % receptor+ target cells; Wilcoxon DE (KIR+CD8 vs other CD8, CeD patients).

REFERENCE AXIS CONFIRMED (excluded from the answer by construction)
MHC-I:KIR was the top-scoring axis in the focus set (CD4_act->KIR_CD8 B2M:KLRD1 magnitude_rank 0.0034, B2M:KIR3DL1 0.0051, B2M:KIR2DL3 0.0106 in the CeD-only run), and KIR3DL1 was the most KIR+CD8-enriched gene in CeD (53.7% CeD vs 18.9% HC positive). This validates the pipeline before asking what lies beyond MHC-I.

TOP NON-MHC-I PATHWAYS PREDICTED TO MEDIATE SUPPRESSION AND CYTOTOXIC TARGETING

1) MHC class II (HLA-DP/DR/DQ) : CD4  - KIR+CD8 -> pathogenic CD4
   Ligand prevalence in KIR+CD8 (CeD): HLA-DPA1 61.2%, HLA-DPB1 60.3%, HLA-DRB1 22.5%, HLA-DQB1 10.1%; receptor CD4 on 100% of activated CD4 cells. LIANA magnitude_rank 0.38 (all samples) / 0.45 (CeD-only), CellPhoneDB permutation p < 1e-3. HLA-DPA1 (score 16.1) and HLA-DPB1 (15.9) are among the most highly enriched genes in KIR+CD8 vs other CD8 T cells (BH-adj p ~ 0). Mechanism: MHC-II on the KIR+CD8 cell engages the CD4 co-receptor/TCR complex of the gliadin-reactive CD4 cell - a suppressor-APC-like interaction that complements MHC-I:KIR and provides the antigen-specific interface for the suppressive phenotype seen in vitro.

2) CCL5/CCL4 : CXCR3 (CC-chemokine axis) - KIR+CD8 -> pathogenic CD4
   CCL5 in 98.8% of KIR+CD8 cells (top-5 DE gene, score 32.1), CCL4 in 76.4%; CXCR3 on 17.9% of activated CD4 cells. LIANA magnitude_rank 0.281 (best secreted axis), CellPhoneDB p < 1e-3. Mechanism: positions/recruits CXCR3+ Th1-type gliadin-reactive CD4 cells and stabilises cell-cell contact so that KIR/MHC-II engagement and granule delivery can occur; CCL4 also signals through CCR5.

3) TGFB1 : TGFBR2 - KIR+CD8 -> pathogenic CD4
   TGFB1 in 52.6% of KIR+CD8 cells (DE score 11.6, BH-adj p < 0.01), TGFBR2 on 22.6% of activated CD4 cells; LIANA magnitude_rank 0.488, p < 1e-3. Mechanism: canonical contact-dependent immunosuppression of the target CD4 cell - the strongest classical suppressive cytokine axis detected.

4) CD48 : CD2 and CD58 : CD2 (bidirectional adhesion/costimulation)
   CD48 68.4% / CD58 15.8% on KIR+CD8; CD2 73.1% on activated CD4 (and 60% on KIR+CD8). LIANA magnitude_rank 0.77 (CD48:CD2) and 0.69 (CD58:CD2), p < 1e-3. Mechanism: high-affinity adhesion and costimulatory signalling that builds the immunological synapse between the KIR+CD8 cell and its CD4 target.

5) Cytotoxic execution - perforin/granzyme dominant, death-receptor and NKG2D minor
   GZMB 82.2%, PRF1 91.2%, GNLY 81.3% in KIR+CD8 (CeD), all strongly enriched vs other CD8 T cells (scores 31.4/31.6/31.8); FAS on 17.2% of activated CD4 cells. FASLG (7.3%) and TNFSF10/TRAIL (7.2% vs TNFRSF10B 2.8%) are low; NKG2D (KLRK1) is ~0% on CD4 cells and NKG2D-ligands are rare in KIR+CD8 (MICA 1.6%, MICB 3.6%, ULBP2 0.4%; ULBP1 absent from the gene list), so granzyme-mediated killing of CD4 targets via synapse delivery (assisted by CD48:CD2 adhesion) is the supported cytotoxic route; NKG2D-ligand recognition of CD4 cells is NOT supported.

6) Secondary/supporting signals (reported for completeness)
   - GRN : TNFRSF1A/B (best raw non-MHC magnitude_rank 0.023 but CellPhoneDB p = 0.43-1.0, low lr_means 0.31) - anti-inflammatory/tissue-repair modulation of TNF signalling; not statistically significant after permutation.
   - HLA-E : KLRC1 (NKG2A)/CD94 on the KIR+CD8 cell itself (HLA-E in 99.3% of KIR+CD8, KLRC1 10.8%) and B2M:LILRB1 - inhibitory self-inputs that tune the KIR+CD8 cell's activation threshold rather than acting on the CD4 cell.
   - HLA-DPA1/DPB1 : LAG3 appears only in the CD4_T->KIR_CD8 direction at low rank and was not significant.

DISEASE CONTEXT
Within CeD biopsies the same axes hold with the same ordering (CeD-only run: B2M:KIR3DL1/2DL3 first, then MHC-II:CD4, CCL5:CXCR3). KIR+CD8 cells from CeD patients are more armed than those from controls: PRF1 91.2% vs 75.5%, GZMB 82.2% vs 71.0%, CCL4 76.4% vs 52.3%, KLRC2 27.5% vs 14.6%, LILRB1 20.4% vs 13.2%, KIR3DL1 53.7% vs 18.9%. Population frequencies did not differ (KIR+CD8 1.58% CeD vs 2.37% HC, Mann-Whitney p = 0.61; activated CD4 1.13% vs 0.56%, p = 0.26; n = 6 vs 4).

CONCLUSION
Beyond MHC-I:KIR, the predicted suppressive interface between KIR+CD8 T cells and pathogenic CD4 T cells in active celiac lesions is dominated by (1) MHC class II (HLA-DP > HLA-DR/DQ) on the KIR+CD8 cell engaging CD4, (2) the CCL5/CCL4:CXCR3 chemokine axis that brings the two cells together, (3) TGFB1:TGFBR2 contact-dependent suppression, and (4) CD48/CD58:CD2 synapse adhesion, with (5) perforin/granzyme-B (rather than FASL/TRAIL or NKG2D-ligand) execution of cytotoxic targeting of the CD4 cells.

LIMITATIONS
Count matrices carry no TCR/gliadin-tetramer data, so pathogenic CD4 cells are proxied by HLA-DR+ activated CD4 cells; mRNA is not protein and dissociated biopsies provide no spatial proof of contact; n = 6 vs 4 gives no power for abundance claims; the dataset lacks myeloid/epithelial/B/stromal compartments, so the wider celiac communication network is not modelled; several axes (XCL1:XCR1, IL15:IL2RB, FASLG:FAS, LGALS9:HAVCR2, MICA/B:KLRK1) fell below the 10% expression-prevalence filter and are quantified only at cell level; ULBP1 is absent from the gene list; KIR-gene percentages confound donor KIR genotype with regulation.

Analysis trace with all code, intermediate tables and figure: ./trace.md (module outputs in ced_scRNA/output/tables/, figure ced_scRNA/output/figures/fig_kir_cd4_communication.png).
grader_notes: The analysis is strong overall with correct implementation of QC, normalization, integration, LR inference, and interpretation, but falls short of ideal in using detection-based cell gating instead of data-driven thresholds and lacking formal pathway-level aggregation scores.

Under the primary analysis, the G2M checkpoint (MSigDB Hallmark HALLMARK_G2M_CHECKPOINT, 200 genes) is significantly enriched among the DEGs shared between the overexpression (A549) and knockdown (H1299) in-vitro experiments, at the pre-specified threshold p < 0.05.

Evidence:
- Shared DEG set: 1,543 genes flagged "v" as overlapping in BOTH the OE block (3,260 DEGs) and the KD block (5,314 rows / 5,290 unique DEGs) of TS7.xlsx. (The name-based intersection is 1,545; the two unflagged extras do not change the result.)
- Background universe (union of both DEG lists): 7,005 genes, containing 121 of the 200 G2M genes.
- Overlap: 37 G2M genes among the 1,543 shared DEGs vs 26.7 expected under the null (~1.4x).
- One-sided Fisher exact test: 2x2 table [[37, 1506], [84, 5378]], odds ratio = 1.573, p = 0.0171 < 0.05. G2M ranks 3rd of 50 Hallmark sets by nominal p (after MITOTIC_SPINDLE, p = 2.9e-08, and UV_RESPONSE_DN, p = 1.9e-04).
- The 37 shared G2M genes include TOP2A, SMC1A, SMC4, RAD21, BRCA2, PLK4, ESPL1, INCENP, KNL1, ATRX, WRN, LIG3, POLE, LMNB1, CCNT1, TFDP1 and PTTG3P; all 37 are up in OE and down in KD (as are 1,543/1,543 shared genes; Spearman rho = -0.20), consistent with a coherent, bidirectionally regulated G2/M program.

Caveats: the result is nominal (BH FDR across 50 Hallmarks = 0.286) and sensitive to the background universe - it holds with the union-of-DEGs background (p = 0.017) and a KD-only background (p = 2.5e-05) but not with an OE-only background (p = 0.87) or a Hallmark-genes-only background (p = 1.0); no genome-wide list of tested genes was available to define the ideal background.

Conclusion: Yes - G2M checkpoint enrichment among the shared DEGs is supported at nominal p = 0.0171 < 0.05.

NO — Kocuria is NOT significantly associated with poor prognosis in this cohort.

Analysis: lung adenocarcinoma patients (investigation = TCGA-LUAD) with matched tumor-sample
microbiome and RNA-seq/survival data. Inner join of the 667 microbiome profiles and 462
RNA-seq samples on the full TCGA barcode (-01A, primary tumor) yielded 457 matched patients
(173 deaths); 51 of them were Kocuria-positive. A univariate Cox proportional hazards model
was fit for every microbiome taxon, and a taxon was called "significantly associated with
poor prognosis" if HR > 1 and p < 0.05.

Kocuria result (primary, presence/absence coding, one observation per patient):
  HR = 1.126 (95% CI 0.730-1.736), Wald p = 0.592 (log-rank p = 0.592), BH q = 0.95.
  Kaplan-Meier median OS: Kocuria-positive 1,073 days vs Kocuria-negative 1,265 days
  (numerically shorter, not significant).

The conclusion is robust to every coding and cohort variant tried:
  - keeping all 597 microbiome rows (duplicate sample profiles): HR 0.976 (0.639-1.489), p = 0.910
  - log(1+abundance): HR 1.075 (0.858-1.348), p = 0.529
  - above-median-load binary coding: HR 1.040 (0.564-1.919), p = 0.900
  - sqrt(abundance): HR 1.08, p = 0.283
  - raw counts per read: HR 1.012 (1.001-1.023), p = 0.036, but this is driven entirely by a
    single outlier sample (TCGA-05-4402-01A, 199 Kocuria reads, death at 244 days); removing
    that one sample gives HR 0.997 (0.961-1.035), p = 0.878. It also fails multiple-testing
    correction, so it is an artifact, not evidence.

Taxa that DID meet the nominal criterion (HR > 1 and p < 0.05) in the taxon-wide
presence/absence scan (182 testable taxa, 240 events) were: Wickerhamomyces (HR 3.14,
p = 0.012), Rhodotorula (HR 3.20, p = 0.022), Alcanivorax (HR 1.33, p = 0.031), Rhizopus
(HR 2.00, p = 0.032), Bifidobacterium (HR 1.31, p = 0.038), Corynebacterium (HR 1.34,
p = 0.047). None survived Benjamini-Hochberg FDR (minimum q = 0.996), and Kocuria was not
among them.

Bottom line: under the task's own definition (univariate Cox PH, HR > 1, p < 0.05), Kocuria
shows no significant association with poor prognosis in LUAD — its p-values range 0.29-0.93
across all defensible codings, and the only nominally significant variant is an outlier
artifact. The analysis is unadjusted (no age/stage/smoking covariates), observational, and
limited to LUAD, so it cannot exclude small effects (CI 0.73-1.74) or establish causality.
grader_notes: The agent performed a rigorous matched-cohort analysis with taxon-wide Cox models and correct filtering, but its final Kocuria conclusion is wrong relative to the expected significant poor-prognosis result, so criterion 4 is rated C.

DA-13-1 FINAL ANSWER
Question: Which plasma proteins are significantly altered after 6 months of feminizing GAHT, and do the changes differ between CPA and SPIRO antiandrogen regimens?

DATA USED
Raw Olink Explore HT NPX table (666,660 rows; 103 study samples x 5,420 assays; single plate, plate-control-normalized, log2 NPX) plus SDRF phenotype metadata (103 rows). After QC (SampleQC PASS in all study samples; AssayQC PASS), 5,414 proteins were testable in 80 samples: 20 CPA subjects and 20 SPIRO subjects, each with paired baseline and 6-month samples. Four SPIRO samples whose SDRF phenotype contradicted their _0m/_6m ID suffix were adjudicated from the proteomic data (projection on the consensus 6-month-change direction of the 16 label-concordant SPIRO subjects); the ID suffix was supported for all four, and sensitivity analyses under the alternative coding and after excluding these subjects are reported below. Six assays (APOE, APP, CTSD, ELANE, APOD, SBSN) are AssayQC-WARN with SPIRO-arm-only data and were excluded from cross-regimen comparison.

METHOD (in brief; full detail in trace.md)
Per protein: mixed linear model NPX ~ time6 * regimen with subject random intercept (paired design, ML fit). Three contrasts: 6-month change in each arm and the time x regimen interaction (CPA delta minus SPIRO delta). Benjamini-Hochberg FDR across the 5,414 tested proteins per contrast. Cross-checked against per-subject paired t-tests (p-value Spearman correlation 0.96-1.00; betas identical to r = 1.000). Effect units are delta NPX = log2 fold change.

1) PROTEINS SIGNIFICANTLY ALTERED AFTER 6 MONTHS OF FEMINIZING GAHT
- CPA arm: 407 of 5,414 proteins at BH q < 0.05 (24 increased, 383 decreased).
- SPIRO arm: 311 of 5,414 proteins at q < 0.05 (13 increased, 298 decreased).
- 128 proteins are significant in both arms; 127/128 change in the same direction (delta-vs-delta correlation r = 0.925 among shared hits), i.e. the bulk of the GAHT response is shared, with a strong net downward skew.

Strongest shared changes (delta NPX, log2 FC; CPA / SPIRO):
- INSL3 (Leydig-cell hormone, direct gonadal-androgen marker): -5.34 (q = 1.4e-65, 0/20 subjects up) / -1.75 (q = 1.9e-06, 1/20 up).
- SPINT3 (prostate/accessory-gland protease inhibitor): -7.91 (q = 1.8e-48) / -3.52 (q = 8.3e-09).
- EDDM3B (epididymal): -2.67 (q = 1.1e-39) / -1.32 (q = 6.6e-09).
- TEX101 (germ cell): -2.08 (q = 6.9e-20) / -0.91 (q = 1.3e-03).
- Also decreasing in both arms: ACRV1, PROK1, MUC1, MMP3, CA6, DEFB4A/B, MYH1 and many other androgen/prostate/epididymis-dependent proteins (383 CPA and 298 SPIRO significant decreases in total).
- Increases in both arms: LEP/leptin +1.50 CPA (q = 8.8e-10) / +1.04 SPIRO (q = 5.0e-04, 16/20 up); GH1 +1.09 / +1.25; SHBG +0.28 / +0.30 (both p ~ 0.015-0.019, not FDR-significant at q ~ 0.08-0.10); FBXL7 +2.96 in SPIRO (q = 3.8e-03).
Biological interpretation: collapse of gonadal androgen production (INSL3) and loss of androgen-dependent male accessory-gland/germ-cell secreted proteins (SPINT3, EDDM3B, TEX101, ACRV1, PROK1), together with an estrogen-driven metabolic/endocrine shift (leptin, growth hormone, SHBG upward) - the expected systemic signature of estradiol plus anti-androgen therapy. Context checks: after 6 months on CPA, INSL3 (-3.8) and SPINT3 (-6.1) reach the levels seen in the cis-female control (-5.3, -5.8) and pregnancy comparator (-5.4, -4.8), and PRL rises toward the pregnancy pattern.

2) DO THE CHANGES DIFFER BETWEEN CPA AND SPIRO? YES - FOR A SPECIFIC, ROBUST SUBSET
24 of 5,414 proteins show a significant time x regimen interaction (BH q < 0.05). Because 4 SPIRO samples had conflicting phenotype labels, I bracketed the result: after excluding those subjects (or using the alternative label coding), 7 proteins remain significant under the strictest analysis. These 7 are the robust differential set (CPA delta vs SPIRO delta; negative difference = stronger decrease on CPA):
- INSL3: -5.34 vs -1.75; difference -3.60 NPX, q = 3.0e-13.
- SPINT3: -7.91 vs -3.52; difference -4.39, q = 4.8e-06.
- PRL (prolactin): +1.38 vs +0.19 (n.s.); difference +1.19, q = 4.8e-10; 20/20 CPA subjects increased - a CPA-specific hyperprolactinemic effect.
- EDDM3B: -2.67 vs -1.32; difference -1.35, q = 6.2e-04.
- CXCL13: +1.84 (q = 8.5e-16) vs +0.21 (n.s.); difference +1.63, q = 3.7e-05; CXCL13 is also elevated in the pregnancy arm (+2.3 to +3.0), consistent with an estrogen-linked (B-cell follicular chemokine) response.
- NELL1: difference +0.43, q = 1.5e-05 (CPA-selective increase).
- CFC1: difference +0.73, q = 4.5e-05 (CPA-selective increase).
TEX101 (difference -1.17, primary q = 2.8e-02) is borderline (q = 0.12 in the strict sensitivity set) but shows the same "deeper suppression on CPA" pattern.

The remaining 17 interaction hits (SPOCK1, RTBDN, REN, FCRL5, NOS3, GLIPR1, B3GNT7, OBP2B, CCL28, IGF2R, FCHSD2, CTSO, IGSF21, DBH, GPIHBP1, CPB2, TEX101 under the strict cut) are sensitive to the labeling of the 4 discordant samples and are lower confidence. Notably REN (CPA -0.56 vs SPIRO +0.19, primary q = 2.0e-03) fits spironolactone's mineralocorticoid-receptor antagonism but did not survive the strictest sensitivity analysis.

SUMMARY CONCLUSION
Feminizing GAHT for 6 months produces a broad, largely regimen-shared remodeling of the plasma proteome (407 significant proteins on CPA, 311 on SPIRO; 128 shared with 127/128 concordant direction): profound suppression of gonadal and prostate/epididymal/germ-cell androgen-dependent proteins (INSL3, SPINT3, EDDM3B, TEX101, ACRV1, PROK1) and increases in leptin, growth hormone and (sub-significantly) SHBG. The regimens differ significantly for a small, robust subset: CPA suppresses the androgen-axis markers roughly twice as strongly as SPIRO (INSL3, SPINT3, EDDM3B, TEX101) and uniquely raises prolactin (PRL) and the B-cell chemokine CXCL13 (plus NELL1 and CFC1), whereas SPIRO's changes in these proteins are attenuated or absent. Overall, CPA shows the stronger anti-androgenic (and hyperprolactinemic) proteomic profile.

LIMITATIONS
- The CPA and SPIRO arms are separate, non-randomized subject groups (20 vs 20); each subject is their own control, and baseline levels of the headline proteins are similar between arms, but confounding by co-administered estradiol regimen, age or BMI (not provided) cannot be excluded - "CPA vs SPIRO" differences cannot be attributed to the anti-androgen molecule alone.
- 4 SPIRO samples had phenotype/ID conflicts; 17 of the 24 interaction hits depend on their adjudication (the 7-protein core set does not).
- Only 24/5,414 proteins pass interaction FDR (389 at nominal p < 0.05); absence of an interaction finding is not proof of equivalent effects (limited power at n = 20/arm).
- No clinical hormone measurements, ages or BMIs were available; the 6 QC-WARN assays (APOE, APP, CTSD, ELANE, APOD, SBSN) had no CPA-arm data and could not be compared between regimens; pregnancy/cis-control groups (n = 3 and 1-2) were used only as qualitative reference points.

Full methods, code, intermediate counts and references: trace.md. Per-protein statistics: results/gaht_results.csv; robust differential set: results/interaction_hits.csv; figure: results/volcano_and_concordance.png.

ANSWER (DA-13-5): Do feminizing GAHT-associated proteins overlap with sex-associated proteins identified in the general population?

YES - substantially and significantly, but only partially and asymmetrically.

PRIMARY RESULT
Among the 2,606 plasma proteins measurable on both Olink platforms (universe), 213 changed significantly after 6 months of feminizing GAHT under the CPA regimen (mixed linear models, adj.p < 0.05; n = 20 participants; this is exactly the study's GAHT_effect=1 flag in Supplementary Table 5, and equals the CPA column of Supplementary Table 1; 81 proteins were significant under SPIRO, 35 under both, 259 under either). Of these 213 GAHT-associated proteins, 129 (61%) are strongly sex-associated in the general population (Sun et al., Nature 2023; sex log10(p) >= 100, i.e. p < 1e-100; 768 such proteins exist). Only 62.8 were expected by chance, giving a 2.06-fold enrichment (Fisher's exact OR = 4.22, one-sided p = 6.3e-23).

ROBUSTNESS
- Threshold sweep: enrichment grows monotonically with sex-association stringency - 1.31-fold at sex log10(p) >= 10 (overlap 184/1,717; p = 5.2e-09), 2.06-fold at >= 100 (129/768; p = 6.3e-23), 2.56-fold at >= 200 (108/517; p = 3.3e-26), 4.40-fold at >= 1,000 (36/100; p = 1.6e-16).
- Per regimen: CPA (primary set) 129/213 overlap (2.06-fold, OR 4.22, p = 6.3e-23); SPIRO 52/81 (2.18-fold, p = 5.1e-11); either regimen 152/259 (1.99-fold, p = 4.4e-25); proteins significant in BOTH regimens 29/35 = 83% (2.81-fold, OR = 11.98, p = 6.5e-11).
- Same conclusion with the full 2,711-protein universe (2.05-fold, OR 4.17, at sex log10(p) >= 100, p = 9.9e-23).
- Gradient: the fraction of proteins changing on GAHT rises with sex bias in the general population - 5.4% (sex log10 p 10-50), 8.7% (50-100), 15.5% (200-500), 21.5% (500-1,000), 36.0% (>= 1,000); median |6-month effect| rises 0.115 -> 0.286 NPX across the same strata. Continuous concordance: Spearman rho between GAHT estimates and Sun female-direction betas = 0.184 (CPA, p = 4.9e-12) and 0.361 (SPIRO, p = 4.6e-44); GAHT-associated proteins are far more sex-biased than non-associated ones (median sex log10 p 200.3 vs 24.5, Mann-Whitney p = 6.3e-29).
- Specificity: the overlap is strongest for sex association (2.06-fold) versus age (1.86-fold) or BMI (1.34-fold) associations from the same general-population statistics, and the sex enrichment is the only one that steeply increases with association stringency (2.06 -> 4.40-fold from log10 p >= 100 to >= 1,000, versus 1.86 -> 1.55 for age).

DIRECTION - FEMINIZATION DRIVEN BY LOSS OF MALE-BIASED PROTEINS
GAHT-induced changes preferentially move the male baseline toward the female reference direction (64% of CPA-significant and 76% of SPIRO-significant proteins; sign-test p = 2.2e-04 and 7.0e-06). The overlap is overwhelmingly concentrated in male-biased proteins: 101/102 male-biased GAHT-significant proteins DECREASE, and the median 6-month decrease equals the entire male-female population gap (median ratio of the 6-month change to the population sex gap = 1.00, IQR 0.63-1.61). Flagship examples: SPINT3 -7.90 NPX (~250-fold drop; most male-biased protein in Sun et al., sex log10 p = 10,660), INSL3 -5.35 (Leydig-cell hormone), EDDM3B -2.64 (epididymal), TEX101 -2.09 (testis-expressed), ACRV1 -1.39 (acrosomal), plus MSMB, CRISP2, SPINK2, PROK1; KLK3/PSA is the #3 most male-biased protein (sex log10 p = 10,461) but lacks a usable GAHT estimate here, making the measured enrichment conservative. Estrogen-driven increases appear too: leptin +1.47 (female-biased, sex log10 p = 7,912; adj.p = 2.7e-04) and prolactin +1.40 (adj.p = 5.5e-07).

PARTIAL, ASYMMETRIC OVERLAP - IMPORTANT CAVEATS
- 84/213 (39%) GAHT-associated proteins are NOT strongly sex-associated (e.g., CXCL13 +1.86 with sex log10 p = 5.1; ZP4 -0.59; CLSTN2 -0.55), i.e., a hormone-modulated but sexually monomorphic component exists. (PSG1, sex log10 p = 136, is only weakly sex-associated.)
- Conversely, most sex-associated proteins do not change in 6 months (only 17% of sex log10 p >= 100 proteins); many female-biased proteins (PZP, FSHB, ENPP2, ADIPOQ, FABP4) are unchanged or decline, and 46 proteins change under SPIRO but not CPA (e.g., OMD, HMCN2, CHAD, PI16), indicating that 6 months of antiandrogen-dominant therapy feminizes the proteome incompletely - consistent with androgen suppression as the dominant short-term driver rather than full estrogenization.
- Limitations: no female reference measured in this study (direction taken from Sun et al., a different Olink platform); the female-vs-male beta is missing ("#REF!") for 1,269/2,711 supplementary rows, so continuous analyses used 1,390 proteins; small cohorts (n = 20 per regimen; the study's GAHT_effect flag tracks the CPA arm, with SPIRO results reported separately); BMI adjusted at baseline only (leptin effect may be partly adiposity); 6-month endpoint only; the supplied adjusted p-values were used as provided and models were not recomputed.

CONCLUSION
Feminizing GAHT-associated plasma proteins are significantly and dose-dependently enriched for sex-associated proteins from the general population (about 2-fold overall, up to 4.4-fold among the most sex-biased proteins, p as low as 1e-26), and the therapy moves levels toward female population values - almost entirely by suppressing male-biased (androgen/sex-gland-secreted) proteins such as SPINT3, INSL3, EDDM3B, TEX101 and ACRV1, with female-biased proteins (leptin, prolactin) rising. The overlap is nonetheless incomplete in both directions, so GAHT at 6 months partially, not fully, feminizes the circulating proteome.

Key numbers: universe 2,606; GAHT-significant (CPA) 213 (SPIRO 81, both 35, either 259); sex-associated (log10 p >= 100) 768; overlap 129 observed vs 62.8 expected; fold 2.06; OR 4.22; Fisher p = 6.3e-23. Supporting analyses, tables, and figures: analysis/results/ (overlap_threshold_sensitivity.csv, control_age_bmi.csv, direction_concordance.csv, sex_stratum_gradient.csv, gaht_sex_overlap_proteins.csv, fig_gaht_sex_overlap.png, fig_enrichment_gradient.png); full script analysis/scripts/gaht_sex_overlap.py; complete trace in trace.md.
grader_notes: The analysis is robust and well-documented but deviates from the task's specified top-100 sex-associated protein set, using threshold-based sets instead; this affects criteria 2 and 3 while data handling, directional, interpretation, and source reliability are strong.

ANSWER (DA-13-6): Are GAHT-induced protein changes consistent with those observed during menopause or menopausal hormone therapy?

YES - and in the direction expected from the endocrinology. Six months of feminizing GAHT moves the
plasma proteome in the SAME direction as menopausal hormone therapy (MHT) and in the OPPOSITE
(mirror-image) direction to menopause itself. Menopause is estrogen loss with relative androgen
excess; feminizing GAHT is estrogen add-back plus androgen blockade, so the two exposures should
produce anti-parallel protein signatures - and they do, quantitatively, at three levels:

1) SAME PROTEINS ARE INVOLVED (set enrichment; universe = 2,922 proteins of Supplementary Table 7).
   GAHT-significant proteins (adj.p<0.05; CPA arm n=212, SPIRO arm n=80, union n=258 - identical to
   the paper's own GAHT_proteins flag) are strongly enriched among proteins associated with:
   - MHT: union vs MHT<57 141 observed vs 61.4 expected, fold 2.30, p=2.2e-29;
           union vs MHT>=57 117 vs 43.4, fold 2.70, p=6.6e-30.
   - Menopause (<57): 222 vs 118.0 expected, fold 1.87, p=9.5e-45.
   - Also oophorectomy (fold 2.27, p=5.5e-13), hysterectomy (2.22, p=1.0e-10),
     ln-estradiol in women (2.41, p=1.7e-25), ln-testosterone in women (1.88, p=1.3e-14) and
     ln-testosterone in men (1.24, p=1.6e-06).
   250 of the 258 GAHT-significant proteins are associated with at least one menopause/MHT/
   sex-hormone/surgical-menopause variable; only 8 (ACRBP, CEP164, DBH, FOLR3, GLT8D2, PAFAH1B3,
   RBP1, ZP4) are associated with none.

2) SAME DIRECTION AS MHT (sign concordance among proteins significant in both, exact binomial test).
   GAHT and MHT effect estimates point the same way in 84/109 = 77% (CPA x MHT<57, p=1.2e-08),
   83/92 = 90% (CPA x MHT>=57, p=3.9e-16), 46/52 = 88% (SPIRO x MHT<57, p=1.0e-08) and
   41/43 = 95% (SPIRO x MHT>=57, p=2.2e-10).

3) MIRROR IMAGE OF MENOPAUSE (same test, opposite expectation).
   GAHT and menopause estimates are ANTI-parallel: only 19/179 = 11% same-sign for CPA
   (89% opposite, p=5.8e-29) and 12/73 = 16% same-sign for SPIRO (84% opposite, p=4.8e-09).
   Of the 174 CPA-significant proteins that DECREASE during GAHT and are menopause-significant,
   157 (90%) INCREASE with menopause; for SPIRO, 60/71 (85%). 92 proteins show the complete
   mirror pattern (GAHT down, menopause up, MHT down), including CA6, BPIFA2, IL1RL1, NCAM1,
   CLSTN2, ICAM4, SPINK2, CA14, WFIKKN2, MYOC, IGFBP7, TFPI, AXL, DPP4, LAG3, OMD, PDGFRA, FAP -
   a coherent extracellular-matrix/endothelial/immune module that rises after menopause and falls
   with hormone treatment.

Continuous (all 2,791 shared proteins): Spearman rho(GAHT-CPA, menopause<57) = -0.321 (p<1e-04),
rho(GAHT-CPA, MHT>=57) = +0.110, rho(GAHT-CPA, ln-estradiol women) = +0.215,
rho(GAHT-CPA, ln-testosterone men) = -0.166. A multivariable model of the GAHT-CPA vector on the
Table 7 signatures gives beta = -0.197 for menopause<57 (p~1e-14), +0.105 for MHT<57 (p=1e-04),
+0.098 for ln-estradiol_F (p<1e-04), -0.144 for ln-testosterone_F (p<1e-13), R^2 = 0.06. For
context, two IDENTICAL exposures measured inside Table 7 (hysterectomy vs oophorectomy) correlate
at rho = 0.580 and the two MHT age strata at rho = 0.459, so -0.32 across a cross-cohort,
cross-design comparison is substantial signal.

MECHANISM - two components, both visible in the data:
- Estrogenic component: GAHT-increased proteins are classical estrogen targets - PRL (+1.40 NPX,
  adj.p<1e-04; falls with menopause -0.422, rises with ln-estradiol +0.334), leptin (+1.47; rises
  with MHT and with menopause), SERPINA12 (+1.00; MHT<57 +0.209, ln-estradiol +0.171), NOS3,
  FETUB, CXCL13 (+1.86), and SHBG (+0.28, not FDR-significant here but the classic estrogen-driven
  liver protein; menopause -0.103 adj.p<1e-04, ln-estradiol_F +0.170 adj.p<1e-04).
- Anti-androgenic component: the largest GAHT decreases are androgen/germ-cell/prostate/epididymal
  proteins - SPINT3 (-7.90), INSL3 (-5.35; Leydig-cell marker of gonadotropin suppression), EDDM3B
  (-2.64), TEX101 (-2.09), RBP1 (-2.03), ACRV1 (-1.39), MSMB (-0.67; rises with menopause +0.240).
  Within the CPA-significant set, GAHT estimates correlate -0.41 with ln-testosterone in men
  (p=3.4e-10). Regimens differ as expected: cyproterone acetate (potent progestin/androgen-receptor
  antagonist with gonadotropin suppression) shows the stronger anti-androgenic signature, whereas
  the spironolactone arm tracks ln-estradiol in men more strongly (Spearman rho = +0.277).

CONCLUSION: GAHT-induced plasma protein changes are consistent with - in fact directionally
isomorphic to - MHT, and are the systematic reverse of menopause. Feminizing GAHT behaves, at the
proteome level, like sustained female-hormone exposure with androgen withdrawal: it recruits the
same hormone-responsive proteins (enrichment 1.9-3.2x, p<=1e-04 throughout), moves them in the MHT
direction (77-95% sign concordance) and against the menopause direction (84-89% opposite signs),
and reverses the surgical-menopause (hysterectomy/oophorectomy) signatures as well.

LIMITATIONS: the comparison is cross-table (within-person 6-month change, n=20/arm, vs
cross-sectional reference-cohort associations adjusted only for age and baseline BMI), so only
direction/rank - not calibrated magnitudes - are comparable; the menopause signal comes almost
entirely from the <57 stratum (the >=57 menopause model yields 3 significant proteins and
ln-estradiol in men yields 0); 33/245 CPA- and 11/91 SPIRO-significant proteins are absent from
Table 7 and excluded from overlap tests; raw p-values and participant-level data are unavailable,
so FDR could not be recomputed and confounders such as BMI change during GAHT cannot be addressed;
and "consistency" here means population-level directional consistency, not identical biology
(e.g., leptin rises both with GAHT and with menopause for partially distinct metabolic reasons).
grader_notes: The agent executed a comprehensive and reproducible analysis with correct data preparation, protein matching, and direction determination. However, the concordance quantification deviated from the expected approach by using doubly significant proteins and separate age strata instead of all GAHT-significant proteins with a unified MHT effect, and the agent completely omitted identification and characterization of discordant proteins, a key component of the rubric.

ANSWER — Which sepsis endotyping signatures cluster together based on their score correlations across patients?

METHOD IN ONE LINE
The 35 non-redundant endotyping score columns (3 exact rank-duplicates dropped: myeloid_score = myeloid_z_score, lymphoid_score = -lymphoid_protective_score = -lymphoid_z_score) were correlated across all 3,948 patient samples with Spearman rank correlation, converted to distance d = 1 - rho, and clustered with average-linkage hierarchical clustering (cophenetic r = 0.871, best of average/complete/ward). The number of clusters was set to k = 6 by bootstrap stability (B = 200 patient resamples: mean Jaccard = 1.00 for k <= 6, falling to 0.905 at k = 7), silhouette (0.49-0.54 plateau for k = 2-6) and within/between gap (0.875).

TOP-LEVEL RESULT (k = 2)
All 35 signatures split into two mutually antagonistic axes (mean between-cluster rho = -0.63): a 28-signature INFLAMMOPATHIC/MYELOID-DETRIMENTAL axis vs an 8-signature ADAPTIVE/LYMPHOID-PROTECTIVE axis. Sweeney inflammopathic vs Sweeney adaptive rho = -0.842. PC1 of the rank-scored signature matrix explains 52.5% of variance — a single dominant immune-dysregulation-vs-competence gradient.

THE SIX SIGNATURE CLUSTERS (k = 6)

CLUSTER A — Inflammopathic / myeloid-detrimental axis (19 signatures, mean within-rho = +0.614, mean rho vs 30-day mortality +0.143):
Sweeney inflammopathic_score & inflammopathic_prob, coagulopathic_score & coagulopathic_prob; Yao IN (yao_IN_score); Wong (wong_score); Davenport SRSq & SRS1_prob; Cano SRSq & SRS1_prob; MARS2 (mars2_score); bespoke mod1_score, mod2_score, detrimental_score, protective_score, som_score, myeloid_detrimental_score, myeloid_z_score, lymphoid_protective_score.
Key cross-framework correlations (pooled rho | random-effects meta rho): inflammopathic ~ Davenport SRSq +0.722 | +0.660; Yao IN ~ Davenport SRSq +0.750 | +0.681; Yao IN ~ Cano SRS1_prob +0.783; som ~ Davenport SRSq +0.822 | +0.758; som ~ inflammopathic +0.818; MARS2 ~ Davenport SRSq +0.782; Wong ~ mod1 +0.697; Davenport SRSq ~ Cano SRSq +0.922 | +0.891; detrimental ~ myeloid_detrimental +0.943. ALL of these pairs reproduce with the same sign in all 6 cohorts.
=> Sweeney inflammopathic (+ coagulopathic), Yao IN, Wong severity, the SRS1 pole of both Davenport and Cano, MARS2 and the bespoke detrimental/myeloid axis are ONE shared latent state: neutrophil-driven innate inflammation with endotoxin tolerance.

CLUSTER B — Adaptive / lymphoid-protective axis (8 signatures, mean within-rho = +0.681, mean rho vs 30-day mortality -0.191):
Sweeney adaptive_score & adaptive_prob; Yao IA (yao_IA_score); MARS3 (mars3_score); Davenport SRS3_prob; Cano SRS3_prob & SRS2_prob; bespoke mod4_score.
Key links: adaptive ~ Yao IA +0.856 | +0.816; adaptive ~ mod4 +0.747; adaptive ~ MARS3 +0.732; adaptive ~ Davenport SRS3_prob +0.737; Yao IA ~ MARS3 +0.761. mod4 vs lymphoid_protective = -0.962 (mod4 is essentially the lymphoid-dysregulation subspace).
=> Sweeney adaptive, Yao IA, MARS3, the SRS3 pole and mod4 converge on a lymphoid/adaptive-immunity-competent axis.

CLUSTER C — Myeloid-protective / monocyte module (3 signatures, mean within-rho = +0.673): monocyte_protective_score, myeloid_protective_score, neutrophil_protective_score (meta rho up to +0.938). Caveat: the least portable module — in cohort 'savemore' it flips sign relative to the inflammopathic axis (myeloid_detrimental ~ myeloid_protective rho = -0.71).

CLUSTER D — Neutrophil-granule / MARS4 module (2 signatures, rho = +0.502 | +0.575): mars4_score + mod3_score; weakly tied to cluster A through wong_score (~+0.45). Consistent with a neutrophil/emergency-granulopoiesis program.

CLUSTER E — Yao IC / MARS1 pair (rho = +0.757 | +0.804, same sign in all 6 cohorts, per-cohort 0.74-0.88): yao_IC_score + mars1_score. This coagulopathy-inflammation dimension runs PARTIALLY ORTHOGONAL to the main axis (MARS1 vs Davenport SRSq only +0.21).

CLUSTER F — davenport_SRS2_prob alone (singleton): the SRS2 'intermediate' probability shares almost no rank information with any other signature (max |rho| = 0.15 with cano_SRS2_prob) and is the single most cohort-inconsistent column (its correlation with davenport_SRSq ranges from -0.80 in qns31079 to +0.65 in savemore).

ANSWER (task DA-14-8)

Question: Are the myeloid detrimental genes and lymphoid protective genes correlated within each gene set?

YES. Within each gene set the member genes are strongly, consistently, and significantly POSITIVELY correlated with one another, and this is not an artifact of pooling cohorts, of the set-definition threshold, or of the choice of correlation metric.

Gene sets (defined objectively from the data as the genes with Pearson r >= 0.5 against the shipped framework scores; membership lists are not provided in the files):
- Myeloid-detrimental set: 35 genes - a coherent neutrophil/granulocyte program (LTF, CEACAM8, OLFM4, LCN2, CTSG, ARG1, DEFA4, CAMP, AZU1, S100A12, AQP9, plus ITGAM, TLR8, MAPK14, TYROBP, BCL6, HK3, GADD45A, ...).
- Lymphoid-protective set: 63 genes - a coherent T-cell program (CD3E, CD3G, CD247, ZAP70, FYN, PLCG1, CAMK4, DYRK2, NFATC1, MAP4K1, PIK3R1, SOS1, plus CD79A, KLRB1, HLA-DMA/DMB/DOA, ...).
- The two sets are disjoint (0 genes overlap); 103 of the 201 measured genes belong to neither.

Key quantitative results (3,948 ICU/hospitalized sepsis samples, 6 cohorts):

1. Pooled within-set pairwise Pearson r:
   - Myeloid-detrimental (595 pairs): mean r = +0.498, median +0.513, range -0.005 to +0.904; 594/595 pairs positive (99.8%); 97.5% Bonferroni-significant.
   - Lymphoid-protective (1,953 pairs): mean r = +0.543, median +0.543, range +0.165 to +0.894; 1,953/1,953 pairs positive (100%); 100% Bonferroni-significant.
   - Examples: LTF-CEACAM8 r = 0.87; KLHL2-MAPK14 r = 0.90; CD3E-CD3G r = 0.88; ZAP70-CD247 r = 0.81; PLCG1-CAMK4 r = 0.84.

2. Not driven by between-cohort structure: after subtracting each cohort's mean, mean within-set r = +0.435 (myeloid) and +0.466 (lymphoid); 96.8% and 100% of pairs remain positive. Every one of the 6 cohorts analyzed separately shows positive mean within-set r for both sets (range 0.32-0.70) with majority-positive pairs in all 12 cohort x set combinations.

3. Formal inference: mean within-set r exceeds all 20,000 size-matched random gene subsets drawn from the 201-gene panel, both pooled and cohort-centered (permutation p = 5.0e-5, the floor of the test; random-subset background mean r only 0.15-0.18). Patient-level bootstrap 95% CI for mean r: myeloid [0.486, 0.511], lymphoid [0.532, 0.554].

4. Internal consistency / modularity: Cronbach's alpha = 0.962 (myeloid) and 0.983 (lymphoid). PC1 captures 54.3% and 56.0% of the standardized variance of each set with fully sign-consistent loadings, i.e. each set moves as one coordinated module; PC1 of the lymphoid set is nearly identical to the shipped lymphoid_protective_score (|r| = 0.973), PC1 of the myeloid set correlates r = 0.784 with myeloid_detrimental_score.

5. Robustness: results unchanged with Spearman (mean r 0.47/0.58), in the infected-only subgroup (n = 2,892; mean r 0.537/0.535, 100% positive pairs), and across membership thresholds r >= 0.3 to 0.7 (mean r always 0.39-0.67).

Contrast: the two sets are anti-correlated with each other (2,205 cross-set pairs: mean r = -0.28 pooled, -0.16 cohort-centered; 94.6% negative pooled), consistent with two opposing sepsis immune phenotypes - a coordinated neutrophil/granulocyte (hyperinflammatory, myeloid) program versus a coordinated T-cell/adaptive (protective) program. Directionality is validated against outcome: myeloid_detrimental_score correlates +0.201 with 30-day mortality and lymphoid_protective_score -0.233 (n = 2,939).

Interpretation: the myeloid detrimental genes form one tightly co-expressed neutrophil-module, and the lymphoid protective genes form one tightly co-expressed T-cell module; co-expression within each set is real (replicates in every cohort and survives removal of cohort effects), so each set behaves as a single coordinated transcriptional axis rather than a list of independent genes.

Caveats: bulk whole-blood data cannot separate within-cell co-regulation from shared cell-composition effects (part of the mutual anti-correlation is compositional, neutrophil vs lymphocyte fractions); 426 patients contribute more than one sample, so effective n is below 3,948 and p-values are liberal (effect sizes, not p-values, carry the conclusion); the gene sets were reconstructed from the shipped scores (r >= 0.5 rule), which introduces mild circularity mitigated by the centered/per-cohort/permutation/threshold-sensitivity analyses; and correlation does not establish causal or regulatory direction.

Full methods, code, and intermediate counts: trace.md; machine-readable outputs in myeloid-lymphoid-correlation/output/ (tables: permutation_test.csv, set_membership.csv, withinset_pairwise_correlations.csv; figure: withinset_coexpression.png).

- Site x disease confounding: 44% of controls come from one site (site_7); with site in the model the disease coefficient leans on between-site contrasts. YES. WGCNA identifies robust, interpretable co-expression modules in ALS spinal cord, and five of them are significantly dysregulated in ALS.

WHAT WAS DONE
Data: bulk RNA-seq of postmortem spinal cord (Zenodo 6385747 cohort): cervical n=174, lumbar n=154, thoracic n=52 (380 samples, 203 donors; 300 ALS-spectrum vs 80 controls; 8 sites; 2 sequencers). Pipeline (R 4.4.1; WGCNA 1.73, DESeq2 1.44.0, clusterProfiler 4.12.0):
1) Gene filter CPM>=1 in >=50% of samples of any level: 58,884 -> 16,771 -> 16,759 after symbol collapse; DESeq2 VST (blind).
2) Residualized each gene on RIN, 5'/3' bias, %mRNA, %intronic, log library size, platform, prep, site, tissue (PC1 of VST was r=0.54 with 5'/3' bias and r=0.35 with RIN, so quality drift had to be removed); kept top 5,000 variance genes.
3) Signed bicor network (maxPOutliers=0.05); soft power 7 (first scale-free R^2>=0.85: 0.86, mean k=152); blockwiseModules minModuleSize=30, mergeCutHeight=0.25, deepSplit=2.
4) Module-trait correlations with ALS status, age, sex, level, site, C9orf72, onset site, duration; BH correction; covariate-adjusted lm; per-level replication.
5) Cell-type attribution with Mathys 2019 snRNA-seq marker sets (Fisher exact, BH); GO BP over-representation.

RESULT: 8 modules + grey (855/5000 = 17% unassigned). ALS-associated after BH (ME-ALS r, q; adjusted beta q):
- BROWN (718 genes, microglia; markers q=5.6e-36; GO "regulation of immune response" q=1.8e-52): r=+0.45, q=1.4e-18; adjusted beta +0.069, q=5.3e-24. Hubs NCKAP1L, CD68, DOCK2, BTK, HAVCR2, TBXAS1, TYROBP; contains AIF1/IBA1, C1QA/B, C3, TREM2, CSF1R, ITGAM; highest gene significance: GPNMB +0.51, CTSS +0.50, APOC1 +0.50, LYZ +0.50, ASAH1/HEXB ~+0.50 - a disease-associated, lysosomal/lipid-handling microglia program. Also r=-0.43 with disease duration (stronger in advanced disease) and +0.26 with limb onset.
- YELLOW (621 genes, oligodendrocyte; q=3.8e-44, OR 47.5; GO myelination/ensheathment q=1.7e-06): r=-0.46, q=2.1e-19; adjusted beta -0.072, q=9.2e-27. Hubs GJB1, MAG, MOG, CNP, PLP1, NKX2-2; MBP, MOBP members - loss of an oligodendrocyte/myelin program. Also r=-0.19 with C9orf72 mutation.
- BLUE (730 genes, GO "cellular response to stress" q=1.3e-08, apoptotic regulation; TNFRSF1A/B, OSMR, NFIL3, BCL6, CDKN1A): r=+0.19, q=2.3e-03 (adjusted q=8.5e-05); C9orf72 mutation r=+0.17.
- RED (273 genes, astrocyte markers q=1.3e-18; AQP4 GS +0.33, hubs CNTN1, GJA1, GAN): r=+0.16, q=2.0e-02 (adjusted q=3.0e-03) - reactive astrocyte program; r=+0.33 with disease duration.
- BLACK (143 genes, endothelial q=8.2e-30; CLDN5, VWF, ESAM, ERG, TIE1; GO vasculature development q=1.4e-16): r=-0.15, q=3.3e-02 (adjusted q=4.4e-03) - reduced vascular/endothelial program.
Turquoise (1,129 genes; excitatory+inhibitory neuron markers, GO chemical synaptic transmission q=3.1e-61) shows only a weak negative ALS trend (r=-0.10, q=0.052; significant in cervical only, r=-0.20).

REPLICATION: the two leading modules reproduce in every spinal-cord level - brown: cervical +0.48 (p=1.6e-11), lumbar +0.42 (4.6e-08), thoracic +0.42 (1.7e-03); yellow: -0.44 / -0.50 / -0.42 (all p<2e-03). Results survive covariate adjustment for age, sex, RIN, level, site, platform. kME-GS concordance (brown +0.70, yellow -0.77, both p<1e-100) shows the ALS association is a coordinated module property, not a few outlier genes. Grey module is null (r=-0.01, p=0.87).

KNOWN ALS GENES PLACED IN THE NETWORK: UNC13A (turquoise, kME 0.91, GS -0.21), KIF5A (turquoise, kME 0.88), TUBA4A (turquoise), C9orf72 (blue, kME 0.47), MOBP (yellow, kME 0.75, GS -0.39; oligodendrocyte ALS-risk gene), SOD2 (blue), GPX1 (brown). SOD1, TARDBP, FUS, OPTN, TBK1, NEK1, MATR3, GFAP were expressed but fell below the top-5,000 variance cut.

INTERPRETATION: the dysregulated programs are dominated by glial activation - an upregulated disease-associated microglial innate-immune/lysosomal program (brown) and a reactive astrocyte program (red), with a stress-response module (blue) - opposed by a downregulated oligodendrocyte/myelination program (yellow) and an endothelial/vascular program (black), plus a modest neuronal synaptic decline (turquoise, cervical-driven). This matches the glial-activation pathology expected in ALS spinal cord.

LIMITATIONS: cross-sectional postmortem data cannot separate cell-composition change from within-cell transcriptional change (marker enrichment is not deconvolution); 119 donors contribute 2 levels and 29 contribute 3 (mitigated by within-level replication); PMI/agonal state/medication unmeasured; Mathys markers are brain-derived, with no motor-neuron-specific set; top-variance filter excludes low-variance genes (SOD1, TARDBP, etc.); no protein-level table was provided, so Oeckl et al. 2019 proteomic orthogonal validation could not be executed from the workspace files.

- 439 of 13,958 tested genes reached cross-level meta FDR < 0.05 (393 negative / 46 positive);
  80 genes were p<0.05 with the same sign in ALL three levels (76 negative).
- Direction: the dominant signal is myeloid/microglial inflammatory genes expressed at higher
  levels in rapidly progressing ALS (short duration). CHIT1 and CHI3L1 are secreted
  microglia/macrophage activation markers (CHI3L1 = YKL-40, a known CSF neuroinflammation
  biomarker). A pan-microglia signature only weakly tracks duration (rho -0.13 to -0.28),

- Robustness: results unchanged with log1p(duration) endpoint (100% sign agreement);

- Cross-sectional postmortem tissue: correlation, not prospective prediction; duration is
  onset-to-death, so terminal-state/proximity-to-death effects cannot be excluded.
- Cervical/lumbar/thoracic samples come largely from the same donors (131 donors), so the
  "meta-analysis" is a consistency/replication check rather than independent validation;
  no external cohort or the proteomics file was available for orthogonal validation here.
- Bulk RNA-seq cannot fully separate microglia activation state from abundance.

The individual genes with the strongest correlation with ALS disease duration are the
microglial chitinases CHIT1 (strongest overall, rho ~ -0.5 in every spinal level) and
CHI3L1/YKL-40, followed by a panel of myeloid-inflammatory genes (RAB42, PYCARD, APOC2,
CAPG, APOBR, ITGB2, OLR1, LSP1, LILRA2, SIGLEC7/9, CD68, NCF2, CD37, TREM2, GPNMB, SPI1,
HLA class II, C1QC, PLA2G7). All are negatively correlated with duration — i.e. highest in
fast progressors — making CHIT1/CHI3L1 the leading RNA-level candidate biomarkers of ALS
progression rate in this dataset, with IL17D, CNTFR and MLC1 marking the opposite
(slow-progression) direction.

ANSWER — Task DA-15-8: Genes concordantly dysregulated across spinal-cord transcriptome, spinal-cord proteome, and CSF proteome (ALS vs control)

METHOD IN ONE LINE
Genes were joined by HGNC symbol across (1) the cervical spinal-cord limma RNA-seq DE table (25,389 genes), (2) the Oeckl 2019 spinal-cord proteome table "Protein IDs (>3 values)" (1,929 proteins, allALS vs Con log2 ratio + Student's t-test), and (3) the Oeckl 2019 CSF proteome table "Tabelle1" (292 proteins, ALS vs Con log2 ratio + Student's t-test). A gene was called concordant if it is significant (RNA adj.p<0.05; each proteome p<0.05) and changes in the SAME direction in all three layers.

FUNNEL
25,329 unique DE genes x 1,904 SC-proteome genes x 297 CSF genes -> 59 genes quantified in all three layers -> 38 direction-concordant -> 33 also RNA-significant -> 11 TIER-1 GENES -> 5 robust at p<0.01 in both proteomes.

TIER-1 CONCORDANT GENES (11; ALL up-regulated at all three levels)
(log2FC: RNA / spinal-cord protein / CSF protein; p in parentheses)

1. GPNMB     +2.65 (4.2e-16) / +0.95 (5.4e-06) / +3.53 (1.3e-03)  -- strongest hit; ~11.5-fold CSF increase, 2nd most significant DE gene in cervical cord
2. LGALS3    +1.36 (4.4e-12) / +0.49 (6.7e-03) / +1.77 (2.9e-04)
3. CAPG      +1.35 (9.0e-12) / +0.51 (1.0e-04) / +1.09 (2.0e-04)
4. S100A11   +1.03 (1.8e-09) / +0.45 (1.9e-02) / +0.94 (1.4e-03)
5. SERPINA3  +1.51 (2.4e-06) / +0.64 (9.5e-05) / +1.59 (5.7e-03)
6. HLA-DRA   +1.22 (5.1e-13) / +0.52 (4.8e-02) / +1.34 (7.9e-05)
7. ICAM1     +0.67 (2.3e-04) / +0.44 (1.7e-03) / +0.93 (1.7e-02)
8. SFN (14-3-3 sigma) +1.57 (2.7e-04) / +0.42 (1.1e-02) / +0.61 (6.3e-03)
9. EMILIN1   +0.59 (1.7e-04) / +0.25 (4.7e-02) / +1.85 (2.6e-02)
10. AHNAK    +0.32 (8.0e-03) / +0.46 (2.6e-02) / +1.05 (1.8e-02)
11. FLNA     +0.34 (1.5e-02) / +0.46 (2.7e-03) / +1.01 (5.0e-03)

STRICTEST CORE (survive p<0.01 in BOTH proteomes): GPNMB, LGALS3, CAPG, SERPINA3, FLNA
ROBUST IN BOTH FAMILIAL (gALS) AND SPORADIC (sALS) SPINAL-CORD CONTRASTS: GPNMB, CAPG, FLNA, SERPINA3, ICAM1
=> TOP PRIORITIZATION FOR NON-INVASIVE CSF BIOMARKER DEVELOPMENT: GPNMB (first), LGALS3, CAPG, SERPINA3, FLNA; then S100A11, HLA-DRA, ICAM1, SFN, EMILIN1, AHNAK.

BIOLOGICAL READ
The concordant set is a coherent glial/inflammatory activation program: microglial lysosomal glycoprotein GPNMB, inflammatory lectin galectin-3 (LGALS3), macrophage actin-capping CAPG, acute-phase protease inhibitor SERPINA3, antigen-presentation HLA-DRA, adhesion ICAM1, Ca-binding damage signal S100A11, actin-crosslinking/scaffold FLNA and AHNAK, ECM EMILIN1, and 14-3-3-sigma SFN. Across the 59 shared genes, spinal-cord RNA and CSF protein changes correlate strongly (Spearman rho=0.709, p=4.9e-10), supporting CSF as a readable proxy of cord transcriptional change. By contrast, neurofilaments (NEFL/NEFM/NEFH) are DOWN in CSF and in RNA but UP in cord tissue protein -- an injury/release pattern, not concordant synthesis -- and known CSF candidates UCHL1, MAP2, GFAP, CHI3L1, CHIT1 are not present (or not significant in all layers) in these tables.

KEY CAVEATS
- The CSF table is a pre-filtered p<0.05 subset (292 of >2,000 quantified proteins); absence from the list is not evidence of absence (e.g., GFAP/CHIT1/UCHL1 lack a CSF row here), and CSF-layer FDR control is impossible from the provided files.
- Layers come from different post-mortem cohorts and assays (summary statistics only; no per-sample data), so concordance is cross-cohort replication, not within-subject coupling; proteome p-values are the authors' nominal t-tests.
- Only the cervical level of the RNA-seq dataset was provided, so level-specific (thoracic/lumbar) concordance could not be tested.
- Borderline spinal-cord-protein p-values make some genes threshold-dependent (e.g., HLA-DRA SC p=0.048, EMILIN1 p=0.047, AHNAK p=0.026), whereas the 5-gene core is threshold-robust.

Full per-gene statistics for all 59 three-way genes: three_way_intersection_full.tsv; analysis narrative and code: trace.md.
grader_notes: Strong multi-modal integration and clear biological interpretation, but shortcomings in filtering, ranking, and CHIT1 assessment prevent full marks.
