FINAL ANSWER — Temporal dynamics of the gene-expression response to 8 weeks of endurance training in rat vastus lateralis skeletal muscle (SKM-VL), males vs females (MoTrPAC differential-analysis table, task DA-6-2)

DATA BASIS. 279,002-row training-regulated feature table filtered to tissue = SKM-VL and assay = TRNSCRPT: a complete, balanced panel of 766 genes x 2 sexes x 4 timepoints (1w/2w/4w/8w), 0 missing values. Every gene in the panel is training-significant overall (training_q IHW-FDR < 0.05); "DE" below means timewise p < 0.05 at a given timepoint, i.e. when a training-regulated gene is moving.

1) OVERALL TIME COURSE - FEMALES RESPOND EARLIER AND MORE BROADLY; MALES ARE LATE-EMERGENT
- Female DE-gene counts rise monotonically: 220 (1w) -> 329 (2w) -> 501 (4w) -> 532 (8w), i.e. 70% of the panel is timewise-significant by 8w.
- Male counts start lower and dip before rising: 145 (1w) -> 134 (2w) -> 176 (4w) -> 379 (8w); half the panel.
- Onset: 220 female genes first become significant at 1w vs 145 in males, and for the 402 genes DE in both sexes the female cohort reaches significance earlier in 223 genes vs 77 for males (102 ties). 251 male genes only appear at 8w (vs 84 female).
- Effect sizes are modest and similar (median |logFC| across all gene-timepoints: female 0.25, male 0.21); the sexes differ mainly in timing/statistical strength, not magnitude (among shared genes, male max |logFC| exceeds female in only 42%).

2) SEX CONCORDANCE INCREASES WITH TRAINING DURATION
- Spearman correlation of male vs female logFC across the 766 genes: 1w rho=0.12 (p=1e-03), 2w rho=0.05 (p=0.20), 4w rho=0.57 (p=6e-67), 8w rho=0.71 (p=2e-118).
- Explicit sex-difference Wald tests (|logFC_M - logFC_F| / combined SE, BH-FDR across 3,064 tests) are maximal at 2w (184 genes p<0.05, 26 FDR<0.05) and nearly vanish at 4w/8w (2 and 3 FDR-significant).
- Interpretation: weeks 1-2 are the most sex-divergent phase; by 4-8 weeks the two sexes converge on the same directional program.

3) PREDOMINANT PATTERNS (Gaussian-mixture clustering of per-sex z-score time courses, K=5; BIC-supported shapes)
Female: (i) late-emerging up (z 1.6 -> 4.0, n=154), (ii) sustained up from 1w (z 2.9 -> 3.8, n=102), (iii) weaker late up (n=126), (iv) sustained down (z -1.6 -> -2.8, n=232, largest cluster), (v) flat (n=152).
Male: (i) early-sustained up from 1w (z 2.1 -> 1.5, n=153), (ii/iii) late-emerging up (n=127+172) and late-emerging down (n=176, z ~0 at 1-2w to -2.0 at 8w), (iv) sustained down from 2w (n=138), flat excluded.
Female-pattern x male-pattern assignment is strongly non-random (chi2=455.5, df=9, p=2e-92): genes keep the same direction across sexes but shift timing.

4) SHARED VS SEX-SPECIFIC PARTITION OF THE 766 GENES
- Shared and direction-concordant: 364 genes (48%). Of these, 54% peak at the same timepoint in both sexes, 96% have the same sign at 8w, and female vs male 8w z-scores correlate r=0.84.
- Female-specific (DE in females only): 255 genes (33%).
- Male-specific (DE in males only): 105 genes (14%).
- Shared but opposite direction: only 38 genes (5%) - sex differences are overwhelmingly quantitative (timing/amplitude), not sign reversals (examples of discordance: Tnmd, Col1a1, Tnfrsf12a, Sln, Ndrg1).
- 4 genes never reach timewise significance in either sex (training-level only).

5) THE SHARED CORE PROGRAM = MITOCHONDRIAL OXIDATIVE METABOLISM, PROGRESSIVELY INDUCED
GO:BP over-representation on leading-edge genes (g:Profiler, g_SCS q<0.05): oxidative phosphorylation p=9.0e-07; energy derivation by oxidation of organic compounds 8.5e-06; respiratory electron transport chain 2.2e-05; proton transmembrane transport 3.5e-05. Named shared up-regulated genes: Ckmt2 (female z +4.4 -> +7.9; male +1.9 -> +2.1), myoglobin Mb (F +1.7 -> +7.3; M -0.2 -> +2.2), Mt-co1, Mt-nd2, Mt-co3, Mt-atp6, Hspb6, Prdx2, Vcl, Lgi3, Mgst3, Gpd1l, Bola3. Shared down-regulated genes: Fos (F z -3.9 -> -6.9; M -2.2 -> -2.4), Hsp90b1, Hspa5, P4ha1, Gstm2, Bcat2, Adhfe1, Psap - i.e. repression of ER-stress/immediate-early and related programs while oxidative genes rise.

6) THE FEMALE-SPECIFIC PROGRAM = EARLY, STEEP MITOCHONDRIAL ENERGY INDUCTION + A SUSTAINED FEMALE DOWN-MODULE
- Female-only leading genes: mitochondrial electron-transport constituents Mt-nd3, Mt-nd4, Mt-nd5, Mt-cyb, Mt-atp8, Ndufa2, Cycs, plus Lipe (lipolysis; +0.59 logFC, z=+5.2 already at 1w), Fabp4, Dbi, Tead4, Pitx3. Enrichment: oxidative phosphorylation p=5.8e-08, ATP synthesis coupled electron transport 2.7e-07, mitochondrial complex-I/NADH-dehydrogenase assembly 4.5e-05.
- All 13 mtDNA-encoded genes in the panel are female-specific (7) or shared-with-stronger-female-signal (6); median 8w z of mtDNA genes: female +5.9 vs male +1.7.
- The largest female cluster is sustained down-regulation (n=232; centroid z -1.6 -> -2.8) containing Per2, Prkag3, Mlec, Calm2, Sort1, Nmrk2, Glul, Sh2b2 - attenuation of circadian/glycogen-sensing and related programs.

7) THE MALE-SPECIFIC PROGRAM = LATE EXTRACELLULAR-MATRIX REMODELING, MOSTLY AT 8 WEEKS
- The only enriched male-specific terms are extracellular matrix organization (p=0.016) with genes Fbln1, Fbn1, Cilp, Col1a1, Col5a1, Col5a2, Ecm2, Ltbp2, Abca8a, Abca9, Itm2a - consistently DOWN in males and essentially unchanged in females (Cilp male z -4.5 -> -5.4 vs female ~0; Fbn1 male -2.3 -> -4.1 vs female n.s.).
- Males also show a distinct early-sustained cluster (n=153; e.g. Ckmt1 logFC +4.1 at 1w) but no female-equivalent mitochondrial enrichment at early timepoints.

BOTTOM LINE. SKM-VL gene expression changes progressively, not transiently, over the 8 weeks in both sexes: a shared, direction-concordant program dominated by gradual induction of oxidative-phosphorylation/mitochondrial genes (Ckmt2, Mb, mtDNA transcripts) and repression of stress/immediate-early genes (Fos, Hsp90b1). The predominant sex difference is timing and breadth, not direction: female muscle engages the full mitochondrial oxidative program within 1-4 weeks (33% of genes are female-only, heavily OXPHOS-enriched), whereas male muscle shows a biphasic course - modest early response, a 2-week trough that is also the point of maximal statistical sex divergence, and a late 8-week emergence that includes a male-restricted extracellular-matrix-remodeling (ECM-gene repression) component (14% of genes). Only 5% of genes change in opposite directions between sexes.

CAVEATS. All conclusions are conditional on the 766-gene training-regulated panel (no non-responsive background genes are in the file, so counts/prevalence are within-panel); timewise p-values are used nominally (the table's FDR is the feature-level training_q); sample-size/batch metadata and raw data are absent, so the original model cannot be refit and "female-specific" partly reflects stronger statistical evidence in females at similar logFC; protein/metabolite layers (424 METAB + 80 IMMUNO SKM-VL rows) were excluded because the question concerns gene expression; 72/766 gene IDs are retired Ensembl identifiers without current symbols.

Supporting files: analysis/output/tables/ (DE counts, logFC matrix, per-gene cluster assignments and class labels, GO enrichment), analysis/output/figures/skmvl_temporal_dynamics.png (4-panel summary), analysis/scripts/ (all code), analysis/README.md (methods record).
grader_notes: Overall the agent produced a thorough, well-documented analysis, but it did not implement the required per-gene, per-sex all-four-timepoint significance filter and 4-character directional state encoding, which also impacts shared/sex-specific pattern ranking.

ANSWER (Task DA-6-5): To what extent does endurance training elicit coordinated molecular responses across different organs, and which tissues exhibit the most similar changes?

VERDICT IN ONE SENTENCE
Endurance training produces a molecular response that is genuinely coordinated across organs but modular rather than global: about 30% of the 22,251 training-regulated molecular entities are regulated in two or more tissues, 79% of the 134 tissue pairs show positively correlated effect sizes (median Pearson r = +0.17), and the shared features change direction in agreement far above chance (57% same-sign, pooled binomial p ~ 1e-84) - and the most similar tissues are, in order, the two skeletal muscles (gastrocnemius and vastus lateralis, r = +0.90), the two brain regions (cortex and hippocampus, r = +0.81), and blood and spleen (r = +0.67).

DATA ANALYZED
data/paper_deg.xlsx (MoTrPAC endurance-training rat differential-analysis table): 279,002 rows = (feature x assay x tissue x sex x timepoint) statistics, 20 tissues, 9 omes (transcriptome, metabolome, proteome, phosphoproteome, acetylome, ubiquitinome, ATAC-seq, RRBS methylome, immunoassays), sexes male/female, timepoints 1w/2w/4w/8w. Every row is already significant (training_q <= 0.05, IHW FDR). Effect measure used: the study's timewise z-score (sign-consistent with logFC in 99.997% of rows), averaged over the 4 timepoints and the 2 sexes per feature; 22,251 distinct entities.

1) EXTENT OF COORDINATION
- 6,643 of 22,251 regulated entities (29.9%) are training-regulated in >= 2 tissues; 593 in >= 5 tissues; only 6 in >= 10. Each organ also retains a large organ-specific program (70% single-tissue).
- Directional coordination is highly significant: 98/132 evaluable tissue pairs have sign concordance > 0.5 (median 0.57); pooling all 21,281 shared-feature comparisons gives 56.7% same-direction (chance 50%, binomial p = 5.2e-85).
- Effect-size coordination: 106/134 pairs (79%) have Pearson r > 0 on shared features; 32 pairs remain significant after Bonferroni correction over all 134 tests; r ranges from -0.39 to +0.90.
- Overlap enrichment (conservative background = union of 22,251 entities): 60/136 pairs hypergeometric p < 0.05; strongest adrenal-driven overlaps: ADRNL-SKM-VL 2.4x, ADRNL-SPLEEN 2.0x, ADRNL-BLOOD 1.8x, ADRNL-COLON 1.7x, ADRNL-BAT 1.7x.
- So: coordination is real and widespread, but its strength is organized along organ-system lines rather than uniform; some pairs even anti-correlate (HYPOTH-SMLINT r = -0.39, BAT-SKM-VL -0.33, BLOOD-HIPPOC -0.32).

2) WHICH TISSUES ARE MOST SIMILAR (primary answer; r = correlation of mean timewise z-scores over features regulated in both tissues)
1. SKM-GN - SKM-VL (gastrocnemius vs vastus lateralis skeletal muscle): r = +0.897 (n = 237, p ~ 1e-59), sign concordance 0.94; transcriptome-only r = +0.91; holds in both sexes (female +0.79, male +0.77). The single most reproducible training response.
2. CORTEX - HIPPOC (brain regions): r = +0.807 (n = 25, p = 3e-7), concordance 0.84; adjacent neuro pairs HIPPOC-HYPOTH +0.63 and ADRNL-HYPOTH +0.59.
3. BLOOD - SPLEEN (immune compartments): r = +0.670 (n = 338 shared genes, p = 2e-45), concordance 0.73 - a shared circulating immune-cell transcriptional program.
Further high-similarity pairs: CORTEX-LUNG +0.65; CORTEX-HEART +0.60; COLON-HYPOTH +0.55; CORTEX-SMLINT +0.54; HEART-HYPOTH +0.51; KIDNEY-SKM-VL +0.51; LIVER-PLASMA +0.50 (driven by 182 shared metabolites - liver as source of the plasma metabolome shift); KIDNEY-WAT-SC +0.50; HEART-SKM-GN +0.43 (largest overlap after adrenal pairs, n = 507).

Tissue modules from hierarchical clustering (average linkage on 1 - r, cut 0.75):
- Immune module: {BLOOD, SPLEEN} (mean within-r 0.67)
- Neuro-gut module: {CORTEX, HIPPOC, SMLINT} (0.49)
- Oxidative-fitness module: {HEART, KIDNEY, SKM-GN, SKM-VL, WAT-SC} (0.40)
- Endocrine-visceral module: {ADRNL, COLON, HYPOTH, LIVER, LUNG, PLASMA} (0.34)
- BAT stands alone (large overlap counts with ADRNL/COLON but idiosyncratic direction).
Most "integrated" tissues (highest mean similarity to all others): CORTEX 0.37, HYPOTH 0.34, PLASMA 0.33, LIVER 0.32, HEART 0.31; least integrated: SMLINT 0.10, BLOOD 0.12, COLON 0.14.

3) TEMPORAL DYNAMICS OF THE COORDINATION
- Timewise-significant features follow a U-shape over training duration: 25,959 (1w) -> 25,464 (2w) -> 20,786 (4w) -> 30,888 (8w); 45% of regulated features are significant at only one of the four timepoints.
- Two temporal modes split cleanly by tissue (correlation-based clustering of the 4-point mean|z| profiles):
  * Progressive amplification (peak at 8w): BLOOD (mean|z| 1.79 -> 2.84), SKM-GN (1.72 -> 2.65), HEART (1.72 -> 2.50), BAT (1.35 -> 2.43), SKM-VL, KIDNEY, LIVER, SPLEEN, WAT-SC - the fitness/metabolic module.
  * Early transient (peak at 1-2w, then decline): SMLINT (2.06 -> 1.04), HYPOTH (2.15 -> 1.25), CORTEX (2.30 -> 1.57), HIPPOC, LUNG; ADRNL, COLON, PLASMA are mixed.
- The early and late programs are mostly different molecules: correlation of per-feature z at 1w vs 8w is only 0.30; 54% of features keep the same sign; 11,097 features are strong (|z|>=2) only at 8w vs 4,666 only at 1w. Coordination is therefore re-established in each time window rather than being one static signature.

4) REPRESENTATIVE COORDINATED MOLECULES (named via Ensembl REST ID mapping; directions from the data)
- Broadest metabolites: trimethylamine-N-oxide (TMAO) regulated in 14/20 tissues with matched early kinetics (log2FC -0.5 to -1.7 at 1-2w, normalizing by 4w); N-methylproline (13 tissues), C3-DC carnitine, ectoine, ala-ala (11 each), 5-methylcytosine rising progressively in 10 tissues (8w log2FC up to +0.69).
- Broadest genes: MT-ATP6, GHITM, BST2, NDUFA12, HMGN2 (8 tissues each); COX4I1, EPAS1/HIF-2alpha, PLA2G2A, RNF213, LCP1, PIK3CD, C3, DLST, GSN (7 tissues) - an oxidative-metabolism axis (NDUFA12, COX4I1, MT-ATP6, DLST) plus an immune axis (BST2, LCP1, PIK3CD, C3, NFAM1, TRAF3IP3) matching the BLOOD-SPLEEN module.
- Circulating immunoassay analytes change broadly: FRACTALKINE/CX3CL1 (9 tissues), TNFA (8 tissues).
- The BLOOD-SPLEEN similarity is carried by 338 concordantly positive transcripts (e.g. TINAGL1 z 3.35/1.74, MXI1 2.85/1.74, TSG101 2.68/1.97, SLC25A39 2.11/2.30).

5) ROBUSTNESS
- Transcriptome-only similarity (the one assay in almost all tissues) reproduces the ranking: SKM-GN-SKM-VL +0.91, BLOOD-SPLEEN +0.67, KIDNEY-SKM-VL +0.56, HEART-SKM-GN +0.50.
- An alternative signed effect measure (sign(logFC) x -log10 p), which additionally covers OVARY, TESTES and VENACV (no z-scores), agrees with the primary matrix (Spearman 0.98 over common pairs) and keeps the same top pairs (SKM-GN-SKM-VL +0.84, CORTEX-HIPPOC +0.77, BLOOD-SPLEEN +0.65); pairs involving VENACV/TESTES/OVARY rest on 5-20 shared features and are not interpreted.
- Sex stratification: coordination persists in each sex (median pair r female +0.23, male +0.17; SKM pair top in both), but strength is sex-modulated for some pairs (BLOOD-SPLEEN male +0.59 vs female +0.22).

LIMITATIONS
- The table lists only significant features (training_q <= 0.05), so the full tested universe is unknown; overlap enrichments use the conservative union of 22,251 entities and are lower bounds, and no "fraction of the genome affected" can be computed.
- Similarity is computed on shared significant features only; pairs with few shared features (HYPOTH-SMLINT n = 9; anything with VENACV/TESTES/OVARY) are unstable and n is reported for every pair.
- Feature IDs differ by ome (Ensembl genes vs RefSeq proteins vs metabolite names), so same-gene transcript-protein coupling could not be computed without an ID conversion resource; omes are pooled assuming z-score comparability.
- No pathway/gene-set enrichment was performed (no rat multi-ome gene-set universe provided); module interpretation rests on named molecules and cited mechanisms (Semenza 2016 on HIF-2; Holloszy 1967 on mitochondrial adaptation; Pedersen & Febbraio 2012 on myokine/endocrine cross-talk; Wang et al. 2019 on TMAO; Stanford & Goodyear 2016 on adipose remodeling).
- Timewise p-values are nominal per contrast; the timewise-significant fractions are descriptive, not FDR-controlled.
- Rats under a 1-8 week endurance protocol: extrapolation to humans, resistance exercise, or longer durations is out of scope.

BOTTOM LINE
Endurance training elicits a coordinated, multi-organ molecular response that is strongest and most similar (a) between the two skeletal muscles (r ~ 0.9), (b) between brain regions (r ~ 0.8), and (c) between blood and spleen (r ~ 0.67), organized into an oxidative-fitness module (heart, kidney, both muscles, white adipose), a neuro-gut module, an immune module, and an endocrine-visceral module; the coordination is directionally consistent (57% same-sign, p ~ 1e-84) but temporally biphasic - an early transient brain/lung/gut response at 1-2 weeks and a progressively amplifying muscle/heart/adipose/blood response peaking at 8 weeks, executed partly by different molecules in each window.

FINAL ANSWER — DA-8-2: Interaction effect size between baseline insulin resistance status and peak glucose reduction (protein vs fiber preloaded rice challenges)

Setup
- Data: CGM traces for rice challenges (Rice, Rice+Protein, Rice+Fiber); 167 traces, 38 subjects; 23 subjects completed BOTH Rice+Protein and Rice+Fiber (42 and 43 replicate traces averaged per subject/condition).
- Outcome: peak glucose increment above each trace's own pre-load baseline (mean glucose over -25 to 0 min; peak over 0-170 min).
- Insulin resistance (IR) status: HOMA-IR = fasting glucose (mg/dL) x fasting insulin (uU/mL)/405; IR+ defined as HOMA-IR >= 2.5 (6 IR+, 17 IR-; fasting labs complete in all 23).
- Contrast: (Protein - Fiber) peak increment within subject; "peak glucose reduction protein vs fiber" is the negative of this contrast.

Primary result (2x2 interaction)
- 2x2 cell means of peak increment (mg/dL, mean +/- SD):
  IR-: Fiber 54.96 +/- 32.76, Protein 52.03 +/- 26.06
  IR+: Fiber 81.79 +/- 29.25, Protein 77.05 +/- 23.77
- Interaction (difference-in-differences) = -4.74 - (-2.93) = -1.81 mg/dL
  i.e., IR+ subjects' protein-vs-fiber peak-increment advantage is only 1.81 mg/dL larger (more negative) than in IR- subjects.
- OLS ipeak ~ preload*IR: interaction beta = -1.81 mg/dL (95% CI -41.0 to +37.4; SE 19.43), t = -0.09, p = 0.926.
- Effect sizes: Cohen's d = -0.096; Hedges g = -0.093; partial eta^2 = 0.0002 (Type-II ANOVA F = 0.009, p = 0.926); two-sample t(21) = -0.20, p = 0.841; Mann-Whitney p = 0.919; permutation test (20,000 resamples) p = 0.840.
- Replicate-level cluster-robust model (85 traces, 23 subjects): interaction beta = 0.73 (SE 7.69), p = 0.924 (consistent null).

Context
- Main preload effect (Protein vs Fiber) on peak increment: -3.40 mg/dL (protein blunts slightly more), t(22) = -0.89, p = 0.383, paired dz = -0.186.
- Main effect of IR status on peak increment: IR+ ~ +26.8 mg/dL higher than IR- (p = 0.058) — IR subjects spike higher overall, but the protein-vs-fiber differential is not modified by IR status.

Sensitivity (interaction effect size under alternative IR definitions)
- HOMA-IR >= 2.0 (8/15): DiD = +4.10 mg/dL, d = +0.22, p = 0.621
- HOMA-IR median split >= 1.37 (12/11): DiD = +8.91 mg/dL, d = +0.49, p = 0.254
- SSPG >= 148.5, 75th pct (4/19): DiD = +22.32 mg/dL, d = +1.35, p = 0.023 (only nominally significant cell; 4 subjects, post hoc)
- Continuous HOMA-IR interaction: beta = +1.81 mg/dL per HOMA-IR unit (SE 5.82), p = 0.757 (r = 0.154)
- Continuous SSPG interaction: beta = +0.118 mg/dL per SSPG unit (SE 0.146), p = 0.426 (r = 0.446, p = 0.055, n = 19)
- Raw peak outcome (not baseline-adjusted): interaction beta = 0.46 (SE 26.5), p = 0.986

Conclusion
The interaction effect size between baseline insulin-resistance status and the magnitude of peak glucose reduction (protein-preload vs fiber-preload rice meals) is essentially ZERO and not statistically significant: standardized effect size d = -0.10 (Hedges g = -0.09; partial eta^2 = 0.0002), unstandardized interaction beta = -1.81 mg/dL (95% CI -41 to +37), p ~ 0.84-0.93. Baseline insulin resistance strongly predicts higher peak glucose increments overall, but it does not significantly modify the relative peak-lowering benefit of a protein preload versus a fiber preload in this dataset. Only a post hoc SSPG-high subgroup (n = 4) hints that the most insulin-resistant individuals might benefit relatively more from protein (d = 1.35, p = 0.023), which should be treated as hypothesis-generating. Main limitation: only 23 participants (6 IR+) completed both preload arms; the confidence interval cannot exclude moderate interactions.
grader_notes: The agent's peak metric computation and two-way ANOVA execution are sound, but primary IR classification and the reduction contrast direction deviate from the rubric.

BACKGROUND / METHOD IN ONE PARAGRAPH
The spiker labels are not shipped in data_meta.csv, so they were reconstructed from the CGM data:
per (participant, food, replicate) curve, baseline = mean glucose over minutes -25..-5 and iAUC =
incremental 0-120 min area above baseline; replicates averaged; each food's iAUC standardized
across the 38 CGM participants; a participant is an "X-spiker" when that food's z-iAUC >= +0.5 SD.

averaged to subject level, and each of the 974 metabolites tested by Welch t-test (6 vs 4), with

ANSWER — Baseline circulating T cell populations associated with 1-year overall survival in patients receiving nivo/chemo (anti-PD-1 nivolumab + gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel), PRINCE/PICI0002 phase-2 trial.

COHORT: Of 108 randomized patients, 36 were as-treated with nivolumab + chemo without the CD40 agonist (Actual Arm A1; all Efficacy Population). 27 of these had baseline (C1D1) CyTOF and formed the analysis set (16 deaths; 4 censored before 1 year at days 43/43/163/213). Median OS 467 days; Kaplan-Meier 1-year OS = 0.61. Baseline T-cell markers were tested by univariate/adjusted Cox regression (continuous, per +1 SD), median-split log-rank with KM 1-year OS, tertile dose-response, and alive-at-1-year logistic regression, with BH-FDR control across 7 tested populations.

FINDINGS (ranked; better 1-year OS unless stated):

1) Tbet+ TCRgd+ T cells (% of TCRgd T cells) - strongest overall. Higher baseline = better OS.
   Cox HR per +1 SD = 0.36 (95% CI 0.20-0.67), p = 0.0012, BH q = 0.008; adjusted for age, ECOG, prior chemo HR = 0.34 (0.18-0.64), p = 0.0008. Median split (cut 0.792): 1-year OS 90% (n=13, only 1 death within 1 year) vs 38% (n=14, 8 deaths), log-rank p = 0.007, hi-vs-lo HR 0.24 (0.08-0.74); tertiles 38% -> 63% -> 86%. Retains independent significance in a 4-marker multivariable Cox (HR 0.40, p = 0.017; model C-index 0.78). Also significant in the randomized-A1 set (p = 0.0007) and pooled nivolumab-receiving set (HR 0.63, p = 0.008), but equally strong in the no-nivolumab (sotigalimab/chemo) arm (HR 0.33, p = 0.0001) - i.e., it behaves as a PROGNOSTIC marker of survival irrespective of PD-1 blockade (innate-like cytotoxic gd T-cell fitness).

2) NKT cells (% of leukocytes) - best 1-year separation and the most PD-1-relevant signal.
   Cox HR per +1 SD = 0.42 (0.20-0.90), p = 0.026; adjusted HR = 0.21 (0.07-0.59), p = 0.0029. Median split (cut 0.0164): 1-year OS 90% vs 38%, log-rank p = 0.0036 (BH q = 0.023), hi-vs-lo HR 0.21 (0.07-0.66); tertiles 33% -> 62% -> 100% (zero 1-year deaths in the top tertile). Alive-at-1-year OR = 16.1 per +1 SD (p = 0.056, n = 23 evaluable). Independent in the multivariable model (HR 0.23, p = 0.043). Holds in pooled nivolumab-receiving patients (HR 0.42 median-split, p = 0.013) but is NULL in the no-nivolumab arm (HR 1.04, p = 0.88), consistent with an association more specific to PD-1-blockade-containing treatment (formal interaction test underpowered, p = 0.22).

3) Tbet+ T cells (% of CD3+) - supportive, same direction (higher = better): continuous HR 0.57 (0.30-1.09), p = 0.091; median-split log-rank p = 0.0097 with 1-year OS 81% vs 46%; tertiles 33% -> 75% -> 83%; adjusted p = 0.079. Not independent of NKT (r = 0.78) in multivariable analysis.

4) Ki-67+ T cells (% of CD3+) - RISK marker (higher = worse 1-year OS): continuous HR 1.68 (0.89-3.17), p = 0.11; median-split log-rank p = 0.031, 1-year OS 33% (hi) vs 91% (lo); top quartile HR 10.7 (p = 0.009), 6/7 patients dead within 1 year; adjusted HR 2.32 (1.02-5.32), p = 0.046. Strongly inversely correlated with NKT (r = -0.81). Null in the no-nivolumab arm.

NULL (no baseline association in this arm): HLA-DR+ T cells (% of leukocytes) p = 0.21; HLA-DR+ non-naive CD4 T cells p = 0.42; HLA-DR+ non-naive CD8 T cells p = 0.40 - baseline activated (HLA-DR+) or non-naive CD4/CD8 abundance does not stratify 1-year OS here.

INTERPRETATION: Under nivo/chemo for metastatic pancreatic cancer, a baseline peripheral T-cell compartment enriched for innate-like effector lineage cells (NKT, Tbet+ T cells, Tbet+ gd T cells) accompanies markedly better 1-year survival, whereas a high fraction of cycling Ki-67+ T cells accompanies poor 1-year survival. NKT and Ki-67+ T cells look more nivolumab-specific; Tbet+ gd T cells look generally prognostic (also predictive of OS in the CD40-agonist arm).

LIMITATIONS: single-arm subgroup, n = 27 with 16 events and 9 one-year deaths; hypothesis-generating associative biomarkers only, no external validation; predictive-vs-prognostic cannot be formally distinguished (interaction tests n.s. at n = 80); 4/27 censored before 1 year add classification uncertainty (results directionally stable when counted as failures); the dataset lacks total CD3/CD4/CD8/Treg frequencies and any on-treatment measurement of the Tbet/Ki-67/NKT/TCRgd panel; unmeasured confounders (disease burden, CA19-9, steroids, lines of therapy) cannot be adjusted for.
grader_notes: The agent performed a thorough and mostly accurate analysis, loading and filtering correctly, selecting T-cell features, and applying survival methodology. The only notable deficiency is that the reported log-rank p-values differ from expected due to using >/< median split rather than >=/<, so full marks are not warranted on results accuracy.

ANSWER (DA-9-7): Do circulating immune-cell frequencies correlate with serum protein levels on-treatment at C2D1 in the PRINCE trial?

SHORT ANSWER: No — at C2D1 there is no statistically significant cross-platform correlation between circulating immune-cell frequencies (CyTOF) and serum protein levels (Olink) after multiple-testing correction. The only notable trend is a modest INVERSE association between the frequency of CCR7+ CD11b+ CD27- B cells and the IFN-gamma-inducible chemokines CXCL9 and CXCL10, which does not survive FDR correction.

ANALYSIS SET
- The two platforms share 73 patients with paired C2D1 samples (CyTOF 75 samples/73 patients; Olink 90 samples/90 patients; overlap 73).
- Critically, at C2D1 the dataset contains only 4 of 16 CyTOF cell-population labels (Conventional DC, CCR7+ CD11b+ CD27- B cells, HLA-DR+ Non-Naive CD4 T Cells, HLA-DR+ Non-Naive CD8 T Cells) and only 4 of 30 Olink proteins (CXCL9, CXCL10, IFN-gamma, Soluble PD-1). The remaining analytes are baseline-only (C1D1/C1D15), and the CyTOF MSI epitote file is C1D15-only. The question is therefore answerable for 16 testable pairs.
- After de-duplicating 303 technical replicate Olink rows (IL-10/IL-6/LAMP3, C1D1 only) and averaging the 2 patients with duplicate C2D1 CyTOF aliquots, the merged C2D1 matrix is 73 patients x 8 analytes (n=65 pairs for B-cell/T-cell rows, n=73 for Conventional DC rows).

PRIMARY RESULT (Spearman rank correlation, pairwise-complete, BH-FDR over 16 tests)
- CCR7+ CD11b+ CD27- B cells vs CXCL9: rho = -0.233, 95% CI [-0.451, +0.011], p = 0.062, q = 0.535 (n=65)
- CCR7+ CD11b+ CD27- B cells vs CXCL10: rho = -0.222, 95% CI [-0.442, +0.023], p = 0.076, q = 0.535 (n=65)
- All other 14 pairs: |rho| <= 0.164, p >= 0.19 (e.g., HLA-DR+ Non-Naive CD8 T cells vs Soluble PD-1 rho = +0.164, p = 0.19; Conventional DC vs Soluble PD-1 rho = -0.152, p = 0.20)
- NO pair is significant at nominal p < 0.05 or BH q < 0.05 (minimum q = 0.535).

SENSITIVITY ANALYSES (all support the null)
1) log10-log10 Pearson: same pattern (B cells x CXCL9 r = -0.265, p = 0.033, q = 0.42; all q >= 0.42).
2) Arm-stratified (A1 GEM/NP/nivolumab, B2 GEM/NP/sotigalimab, C2 triple): B-cell x CXCL9 direction consistent in all three arms (rho = -0.138 / -0.330 / -0.399), none individually significant at n = 21-23.
3) Arm-adjusted partial Spearman: B cells x CXCL9 rho = -0.273 (p = 0.028); B cells x CXCL10 rho = -0.213 (p = 0.088) — the trend is not arm-driven but still fails multiplicity correction.
4) Paired C1D1 -> C2D1 change analysis (n = 53-54 cross-platform): no correlation between on-treatment changes in cell frequencies and protein changes (all |rho| <= 0.13, q >= 0.95). The proteins themselves rise on treatment (median dNPX, Wilcoxon: Soluble PD-1 +1.04, p = 7.7e-9; IFN-gamma +0.95, p = 1.7e-5; CXCL10 +0.27, p = 7.7e-4; CXCL9 +0.16, p = 0.031; n = 71) while the paired cell populations do not shift (all p >= 0.14, n = 54).
5) Baseline benchmark at C1D1 (78 patients, 364 testable pairs from 13 populations x 28 proteins): the same pipeline DOES detect cross-platform structure — HLA-DR+ T cells x IL-8 (rho = -0.433, q = 0.030) and Tbet+ T cells x IL-8 (rho = -0.413, q = 0.035), with a near-threshold myeloid-suppression cluster (CD14+ HLA-DRlo m-MDSC x IL-10 rho = +0.406, q = 0.052; m-MDSC x CAH9; HLA-DR+ T x HGF; NKT x HCLS1). Those analytes are absent at C2D1 in this dataset.

INTERPRETATION
- For the analytes measurable at C2D1, circulating cell frequencies and serum proteins vary largely independently across patients on treatment; the on-treatment IFN-gamma/PD-1 proteomic response is not mirrored by (or correlated with) the four on-treatment CyTOF populations.
- The B-cell x CXCL9/CXCL10 inverse trend is biologically coherent (CXCL9/CXCL10 are myeloid-derived IFN-gamma-inducible CXCR3 ligands, so an inverse relation with a circulating activated/terminally-differentiated B-cell subset is plausible) and direction-consistent across arms, but with n = 65 it remains a hypothesis-generating signal, not a validated correlation.

LIMITATIONS
- The C2D1 conclusion covers only 4 cell populations x 4 proteins; the trial's MDSC, pDC, Ki-67+ T, Tbet+ T, NKT populations and 24 additional serum proteins are simply not present at C2D1 in this data release, so nothing can be said about them on-treatment.
- Power: with n = 65-73, only correlations of roughly |rho| >= 0.35 would be detected reliably; moderate true correlations could be missed.
- Cross-sectional correlation cannot establish causality or mechanism; arm adjustment cannot remove all treatment-related heterogeneity.
